# **Definition and Acronyms**  {#definition-and-acronyms}

| \# | Acronym | Definition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | GMS | Gym Management System — the system described in this document |
| 2 | SRS | Software Requirement Specification |
| 3 | PT | Personal Trainer |
| 4 | UC | Use Case |
| 5 | BF | Business Flow (main business flows in section 2\) |
| 6 | GBR | General Business Rule — applies to the whole system |
| 7 | CBR | Common Business Rule — shared by several use cases |
| 8 | BR | Business Rule — belongs to one use case |
| 9 | DBR | Data Business Rule — rule about data format, uniqueness, states and derived values |
| 10 | MSG | System message code (MSG01–MSG105, section System Messages) |
| 11 | P-xx | System parameter configured by the Manager or at deployment (P-01–P-21) |
| 12 | JOB-xx | Background job that runs on a schedule without user action |
| 13 | API | Application Programming Interface — an external service called by or calling the system |
| 14 | ERD | Entity Relationship Diagram |
| 15 | NFR | Non-Functional Requirement |
| 16 | VAT | Value Added Tax, already included in catalogue prices |
| 17 | VND | Vietnamese dong, the only currency used |
| 18 | IPN | Instant Payment Notification — the call VNPay makes to report a payment result |
| 19 | VNPay | Online payment gateway used for online payments |
| 20 | SMTP | Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — used to send verification codes and notifications by email |
| 21 | Person | The real individual behind every profile; one Person has one phone number, one email and at most one login account |
| 22 | Role | What a Person works as after signing in: Customer, PT, Receptionist, Manager or Admin |
| 23 | Membership package | A package that grants gym access for a number of months |
| 24 | Day pass | A package that grants a single entry on one day |
| 25 | PT package | A package of PT sessions sold by term (1, 2 or 3 months), single or couple |
| 26 | Single session | One PT session bought on its own |
| 27 | Freeze | Pausing a membership package for a period; the frozen days are added to its end date |
| 28 | Slot | A time on a PT's calendar that can hold one session (90 minutes) |
| 29 | Dependent | A customer profile without its own phone number, reached through a guardian |
| 30 | Soft delete | Deleting by switching a record to Inactive instead of removing it from the database |
| 31 | Audit log | The record of sensitive actions: who did what, to what, when and why |
| 32 | Shift | A Receptionist work shift (Morning or Afternoon) in which counter payments are recorded |

## **2\. Main Business Flow** {#2.-main-business-flow}

### **2.1 Single PT Session (BF-01)** {#2.1-single-pt-session-(bf-01)}

**Trigger**: A customer books a single session online, or a walk-in guest purchases a single session for today at the counter. The session date must fall within an active membership or a valid day pass.   

**End condition**: The session reaches the final state of Completed, Missed (quota deducted), or Cancelled.

![][image3]

###  **2.2 Membership Package Purchase & Usage (BF-02)** {#2.2-membership-package-purchase-&-usage-(bf-02)}

**Online flow**

**Trigger:**

1. Customer logs in to the system.  
2. Customer browses membership or day packages.  
3. Customer clicks "Buy Now".

**End condition:**

1. Success: payment succeeds and amount matches, order is Paid, subscription is created, customer sees success message.  
2. Overdue: no successful payment before the order deadline, order is cancelled (Overdue), voucher usage is released, customer can buy again.  
3. Invalid payment: money arrives for a cancelled order or amount does not match, order is cancelled, no subscription is created, payment is added to the refund list.

**![][image4]**

[**Link**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1N-k_VrNY8sdN-tStpDI1sJT-GE-t-M9c/view?usp=sharing)

**Offline flow (at the front desk)**

**Trigger:**

1. Customer comes to the front desk to buy a membership or day package.  
2. Receptionist searches the customer profile by phone number.

**End condition:**

1. Success: payment is confirmed, order is Paid, subscription is created, check-in photo is taken if required.  
2. Cancelled: payment is not received, receptionist cancels the order.  
3. Not eligible: customer cannot purchase the package, system shows the reason.

**![][image5]**

### **2.4 Customer Onboarding & Identity Resolution (BF-04)** {#2.4-customer-onboarding-&-identity-resolution-(bf-04)}

**Trigger**: A customer profile is created by the Receptionist at the counter or through customer self-registration online. 

**End condition**: Both pathways converge into exactly one unique Customer Code, and the login account is correctly linked to that profile. 

![][image6]

### **2.5 Staff Leave Request Approval (BF-05)** {#2.5-staff-leave-request-approval-(bf-05)}

**Trigger**: PT/Receptionist opens the application for leave.

**End condition**:   Approved

Rejected by Manager

Rejected automatically because approval is overdue

Blocked immediately upon submission

![][image7]

### **2.6 Facility Maintenance Request Approval  (BF-06)** {#2.6-facility-maintenance-request-approval-(bf-06)}

**Trigger:** The receptionist finds a facility item broken.

**End conditions:**

1. **Closed:** The Manager approved the request, the repair was done, and the receptionist verified the item is usable and closed the request.  
2. **Rejected:** The Manager rejected the request and entered the required reason. The system sets the status to Rejected and notifies the receptionist.

![][image8]

### **2.7 Member Deletion Approval (BF-07)** {#2.7-member-deletion-approval-(bf-07)}

**Trigger**: The receptionist selects the client's profile, clicks Delete, and enters a reason.

**End condition**:   

The profile becomes Inactive with a deletion time (soft delete, GBR-05); orders, transactions, subscriptions, check-ins and sessions are kept unchanged. Every session of the Person's account is signed out; the account stays Active if the Person still has a non-Inactive role, otherwise it becomes Inactive (CBR-86). The phone number and email are released only when every role of the Person is Inactive (DBR-28). This happens immediately, with an audit log entry and no deletion request, when nothing remains (BR-15), or after the Manager approves the Pending request (CBR-16).

![][image9]

### **2.8 PT Package Session (BF-08)** {#2.8-pt-handled-session-rescheduling-&-cancellation-(bf-08)}

**Trigger**: A PT package order (single or couple) becomes Paid and its sessions are generated as Scheduled (CBR-50). This workflow covers the lifecycle of package sessions; SingleSession purchasing is covered by BF-01.

**Main flow**:

1. The Receptionist sells the PT package (UC-21). On successful payment, the system generates one Scheduled session for every Monday-to-Friday within the package term (BR-40).
2. On the session day, the customer checks in at the counter; the Receptionist records the gym visit (UC-19).
3. The PT teaches without entering attendance or absence data in the system.
4. In the daily job chain beginning at 00:05 the next day, JOB-04 processes sessions still Scheduled with a session date before today. It checks gym access and the check-in history for the session date, then sets CheckedIn when the customer qualifies. For a couple package, one member with valid gym access and a check-in is sufficient.

**Alternative flows**:

- **A1 — Customer absent**: No eligible customer checked in on the session date. JOB-04 sets Missed with MissedReason = NoCheckIn.
- **A2 — PT handles the session before its start**: After agreeing outside the system, the PT reschedules, transfers or cancels the session, or changes the schedule on behalf of a customer without an account (UC-35). The four options are detailed below. A move returns the session to Scheduled; it is later closed through the main flow or another final-state branch.
- **A3 — Customer swaps**: The customer swaps an eligible package session to a published free weekend slot (UC-38), subject to the package's remaining swap allowance, target-date eligibility and self-service booking window. The session remains Scheduled.
- **A4 — Customer cancels**: The session becomes Cancelled with CancelType = ByCustomer, remains deducted and is not refunded (UC-39, BR-79).

**Exceptions**:

- **E1 — No gym access**: JOB-04 sets Missed / NoMembership if the customer, or both members of a couple package, has no eligible gym access on that date (CBR-64). For this implementation, valid Membership or DayPass counts as gym access, as subsequently agreed in the project discussion.
- **E2 — Membership frozen**: Saving a freeze marks affected Scheduled sessions Missed / MembershipFrozen (CBR-62). A couple session stays Scheduled if the other member remains eligible (CBR-67). These final sessions are not processed again by JOB-04.
- **E3 — PT package expired**: JOB-02 cancels remaining Scheduled sessions with CancelType = PackageExpired (CBR-55).

**End condition**: Each session ultimately becomes CheckedIn, Missed or Cancelled. These states are final (DBR-38); a successful reschedule or transfer is an intermediate step, not the end of BF-08.

**Known limitation**: CheckedIn means the customer visited the gym on the session date. It does not prove that the customer trained with the PT. A customer who checked in but skipped PT can still be classified as CheckedIn.

**A2 detail — PT session handling (UC-35)**:

The PT cannot teach and agrees on a handling option with the customer outside the system (BR-63), or a customer without an account asks for a change (BR-62). For a Dependent profile, the PT verifies the guardian's phone number before proceeding.

**Common eligibility**: Only the PT assigned to the selected session may act. The session must still be Scheduled and its start time must be in the future (BR-69, BR-70). The system checks these conditions again when saving; opening the screen does not reserve the right to change the session.

**Handling steps**:

1. The PT selects a session and one of the four options below.
2. The system checks the PT's authority, session status and start time, then validates the selected option and its required data.
3. For a move, the target slot must be free, belong to the selected PT and lie within the package term. The target date must satisfy CBR-61: the customer, or at least one member of a couple package, has valid membership on that date. Customer self-service restrictions must not be applied to PT rescheduling or transfer (CBR-39, CBR-45).
4. The system saves the session change, affected slot states, move history and any swap counter change together. If a condition fails or the target slot is no longer available, nothing is changed.
5. After successful handling, the customer is notified; both members are notified for a couple package where they have accounts. A transfer also notifies the receiving PT. A Dependent profile has no in-system notification channel.

| Option | Result | Swap allowance / money |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Reschedule because the PT is unavailable | Move to another free slot of the same PT; remain Scheduled. Record SessionMoveLogs.MoveType = PtReschedule. | No session is deducted and SwapsUsed is unchanged (BR-64). |
| Transfer PT | Move to a free slot of another PT available at the session time; remain Scheduled. Record MoveType = PtTransfer. | No session is deducted; SwapsUsed is unchanged. Keep the session value; commission belongs to the receiving PT. No additional charge or refund (BR-65, BR-68). |
| Cancel by PT | Require a reason and confirmation that the customer agreed to a cash refund. Set Cancelled with CancelType = ByPt and release the future slot. | The session remains deducted and commission is still earned. The PT returns cash outside the system; no refund transaction is created (BR-66, BR-67, BR-71). |
| Change at the request of a customer without an account | Verify the requester; move to another published free slot of the same PT within the package term. Remain Scheduled and record MoveType = PtOnBehalfSwap. | Increase SwapsUsed by one. Require SwapsUsed < MaxSwapsSnapshot, copied from P-08 at sale (default 3). SingleSession cannot use this option. Unlike customer self-service, this option is not limited to weekend slots or the current/next week (BR-62, BR-73, BR-74). |

**A2 outcomes**:

1. **Session Handled**: One option is saved successfully with the corresponding slot, history, counter and notification updates above. A move returns to Scheduled; cancellation ends the session.
2. **Action Denied**: Nothing changes when the actor is not the assigned PT, the session is no longer Scheduled or has started, requester verification fails, required data is missing, the target is invalid/unavailable, or the on-behalf swap is ineligible or has reached its package limit. A session that has already started must be reported to the Manager outside this flow; the Manager does not perform these actions on the PT's behalf (BR-69, BR-70).
3. **Abandoned**: The PT closes the form without saving; nothing changes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P[PT package order Paid] ==> S[Generate Scheduled sessions]
    S ==> D[Session day: customer checks in at counter]
    D ==> J[JOB-04 after the session date]
    J ==> V{Eligible gym access and same-day check-in?}
    V ==>|Yes: one eligible member suffices for a couple| C[CheckedIn]
    V -->|Eligible access but no check-in| M[Missed / NoCheckIn]
    V -->|No eligible access| N[Missed / NoMembership]
    S --> A2[A2: PT handles session before start]
    A2 -->|Valid reschedule, transfer or on-behalf swap| S
    A2 -->|Valid PT cancellation| X[Cancelled / ByPt]
    A2 -->|Validation fails| R[No changes: keep existing session]
    S --> A3[A3: valid customer swap]
    A3 --> S
    S --> A4[A4: customer cancellation]
    A4 --> Y[Cancelled / ByCustomer]
    S --> E2[E2: freeze applies and no eligible partner]
    E2 --> F[Missed / MembershipFrozen]
    S --> E3[E3: package expires / JOB-02]
    E3 --> E[Cancelled / PackageExpired]
```

**Implementation status (09/10/2026)**: JOB-04 is implemented through AutoCloseUnmarkedSessionsJob, AutoCloseSessionService and AutoCloseSessionDAO; it provides the automatic closure in the main flow and A1/E1. The PT Dashboard's four disabled session-option buttons are only the entry-point placeholder for A2; saving those actions is not implemented yet. BF-09 freeze handling and JOB-02 package expiry provide the related exception branches. Their presence in this workflow diagram is not a claim that every branch has been implemented or verified.

### **2.9 Membership Freeze & Auto-Resume (BF-09)** {#2.9-membership-freeze-&-auto-resume-(bf-09)}

**Trigger**: The customer asks the Receptionist at the desk to freeze their membership; the Receptionist enters the freeze period.

**End conditions**:

1. **Freeze Applied**: The request passes the freeze rules. The membership and the customer profile change to Frozen, and all Scheduled PT sessions inside the freeze period are marked Missed (reason: membership frozen).  
2. **Auto-Resumed**: The freeze period expires. The system automatically resumes the membership and the customer profile to Active and extends the membership expiry date by the actual number of frozen days.  
3. **Freeze Denied**: The request violates a freeze rule (not a membership, expired, no freezes left, or duration over the maximum). The system shows the reason and nothing changes.

![][image11]

### **2.10 Day Pass/Walk-in Check-in (BF-10)** {#2.10-day-pass/walk-in-check-in-(bf-10)}

**Trigger:** A walk-in customer requests a day pass at the front desk.

**End conditions:**

> 1. **Success:** The customer checks in; the day pass is consumed and expires immediately.  
> 2. **Order cancelled:** Payment is not received and the customer does not retry; the receptionist cancels the order.  
> 3. **Check-in rejected:** The customer has no valid day pass for today.

> Note: An unused day pass expires automatically at end of day

**![][image12]**

### **2.11  Voucher Application at Purchase (BF-11)** {#2.11-voucher-application-at-purchase-(bf-11)}

**Trigger**: Customer/Receptionist enter the voucher code on the payment screen or the counter order creation screen.

**End condition**:   

Applied successfully, usage count \+1.   

Rejected with a reason. 

Remove / change code → return usage count.

Cancelled order → return usage count. 

![][image13]

### **2.12  Feedback Reading (BF-12)** {#2.12-feedback-reading-(bf-12)}

**Trigger:** A customer writes feedback (10–1000 characters) and submits it from the suggestion box (UC-42).

**End condition:** The feedback is saved as Unread with its sent time. It becomes Read when the Manager opens and reads it in the feedback mailbox (UC-43); the system records the read time. Only the Manager can read feedback, and there is no reply or resolution step (CBR-106, CBR-107). 

![][image14]

### 

### **2.13 PT Regular Check-in & Service Access  (BF-13)** {#2.13-pt-regular-check-in-&-service-access-(bf-13)}

**Trigger:** The customer arrives at the front desk. 

**End conditions:**

1. **Check-in successful:** The customer has a valid gym package or day pass, and any required photo check is done. The visit is recorded, and a day pass expires immediately.  
2. **Rejected with reason:** The customer is not allowed in. The reason is one of: package expired, package frozen, or PT package only. The receptionist shows the reason, and the PT-only case also invites the customer to buy a gym package.

![][image15]

### **2.14 PT Content Delivery  (BF-14)** {#2.14-pt-content-delivery-(bf-14)}

**Trigger**: PT opens the workout plan and meal plan editor screen for a client in their assigned client list. 

**End condition**:   

The client can view the latest published version 

Published: the PT publishes; the client sees this version (Published Title / Content / At). Draft saved: the PT saves edits without publishing; the client keeps seeing the last published version, or nothing if the plan was never published (BR-60). Deleted: the PT deletes the plan; it disappears from My Plan immediately (BR-61). Blocked: the plan belongs to another PT (CBR-91).

### **3.2 Entity Descriptions** {#3.2-entity-descriptions}

**Entity: Person**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | The real human behind every profile. Holds the identity data shared by the Customer and Employee roles, so someone who both works at the gym and trains there is stored once, with one phone number and one email. |
| Key business attributes | Full name, date of birth, phone, email, avatar, released flag, created time |
| Business identity | A Person has at most one customer profile that is not Inactive, at most one employee record with status Working, and at most one login Account that serves every non-Inactive role (DBR-65); an Inactive role does not block creating a new role of the same kind (CBR-114). Phone and email must be unique among Persons that are not released (DBR-22, DBR-23, DBR-27, DBR-30); the phone is empty for a Dependent customer, who is reached through the guardian numbers on the Customer profile (DBR-24). Email is mandatory for anyone with a login account (DBR-23). The avatar is for display only and never used for check-in (CBR-37): JPG or PNG, max 2 MB, 200 × 200 to 2000 × 2000 px, stored as a 256 × 256 centre crop (DBR-64). Customers and staff change only their own avatar, email, phone and password (CBR-30, CBR-108); a new email or phone needs a verification code (CBR-110). |
| Status / lifecycle | No status field. A Person stays held while at least one of their roles is not Inactive; once every role is Inactive the Person is marked released and the phone and email can be reused by someone else (DBR-28). |

**Entity: Customer**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A customer's profile — the member role of a Person — created for every registered visitor, even one who has never purchased anything yet. Name, date of birth, email and avatar are kept on the Person. |
| Key business attributes | Customer Code (system-generated, read at check-in), customer type (Self / Dependent), check-in photo, guardian full name, relationship and up to two guardian phone numbers (Dependent only), joined date, deleted date |
| Business identity | Identified by a system-generated Customer Code (KH-nnnn) that never changes, not by any card or user-chosen ID. At most one customer profile that is not Inactive per Person; after a profile becomes Inactive a new one can be created on the same Person (DBR-65, CBR-114). A Self profile uses the phone number on its Person, which is mandatory. A Dependent profile has no phone of its own (DBR-24) and no login account (CBR-21); an email is optional (DBR-26). It is reached only through the guardian numbers recorded on the profile, which siblings may share (DBR-24, DBR-25). A Self profile has no guardian data. A Dependent profile must have guardian full name, relationship and Guardian Phone; Guardian Phone 2 is optional and must differ from Guardian Phone; both follow DBR-17 (DBR-25). The type cannot change after creation (BR-18). The check-in photo belongs to the profile and only the Receptionist can take or retake it (CBR-35, CBR-38). |
| Status / lifecycle | New (registered, no purchase yet) · Active (has a valid subscription) · Frozen (subscription frozen) · Expired (subscription lapsed) · Inactive (deleted — final state, the profile can no longer be edited; its phone and email are released once the Person has no other active role). Deleting sets Status Inactive and Deleted At; orders, transactions, subscriptions, check-ins and sessions are kept, and revenue reports do not filter out Inactive customers (GBR-05). |

**Entity: Account**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | The single login credential of a Person, shared by every role the Person holds (customer and/or staff). Not every Person has one: Dependents and day-pass-only customers have no account (CBR-17, CBR-18). |
| Key business attributes | Password (stored hashed), status, failed login count, locked-until time, last login time, created time |
| Business identity | Belongs to exactly one Person and serves every role of that Person that is not Inactive (DBR-65). The user signs in with email or phone number; an account with two or more roles chooses the working role on Select Role (/select-role), and the session holds exactly one role that can be switched from the account menu without signing in again (CBR-113). The login email is always the Person's own email — there is no separate email field to keep in sync (DBR-23, DBR-65). Staff accounts are created only by the Admin; customer accounts come from self sign-up or from the Receptionist (CBR-95). If the Person already has an account, no second account is created: the existing account also serves the new role (CBR-24, CBR-95). A Receptionist-created account has no password and no email is sent; the customer sets a password through Forgot Password, and until then every sign-in attempt points to Forgot Password (CBR-31). Role and account status are never editable in Account Settings, only by the Admin (CBR-109). When the email changes, the old email is notified and every session of the account except the one that made the change is signed out (CBR-29); email, phone and password changes are written to the audit log, never the password or code itself (CBR-112, DBR-02). |
| Status / lifecycle | Active · Locked (disabled by the Admin) · Inactive (final; set only when every role of the Person is Inactive — a deleted customer profile or a resigned employee alone does not make the account Inactive while another role remains, CBR-86). A temporary lockout after repeated wrong passwords applies to customer accounts only (BR-01) and is tracked in Locked Until, not by changing Status. |

**Entity: VerificationCode**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A one-time 6-digit code proving that someone controls an email address, for sign-up, claiming an existing profile, password recovery, email change or phone change. |
| Key business attributes | Email the code was sent to, purpose (SignUp / Claim / Recovery / EmailChange / PhoneChange), 6-digit code, sent time, expiry time, failed attempts, locked-until time, used time |
| Business identity | Identified by system ID. Recovery, EmailChange and PhoneChange codes are tied to an Account; SignUp and Claim codes have no Account. Valid for 15 minutes (P-15). For a new email the code goes to the new email; for a new phone number it goes to the current email (CBR-110). A new code always cancels the previous one (CBR-94). |
| Status / lifecycle | No status field — a code is usable (not used, not expired, not cancelled), used, or expired. 5 wrong entries cancel the code and lock verification for that email for 5 minutes (P-17, P-18); a new code can be requested 60 seconds after the previous one, and the 5th request within an hour triggers the same lock (CBR-94). |

**Entity: Employee**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A staff member's profile — the staff role of a Person — covering Admin, Manager, PT and Receptionist in one entity, distinguished by Position. Name, date of birth, phone, email and avatar are kept on the Person. |
| Key business attributes | Employee Code, position, hire date, commission rate (PT only, mandatory for a PT), specialty and years of experience 0–60 (PT only, shown on the home page), employment status, resignation date and reason |
| Business identity | Identified by a system-generated Employee Code (NV-nnnn). At most one employee record with status Working per Person; a Resigned record does not block re-hiring on the same Person (DBR-65). Phone and email are the Person's and are unique among all active Persons, staff included — there is no separate staff phone list (DBR-27, DBR-30). Commission rate is mandatory for a PT and empty for every other position; specialty and experience are allowed only for a PT; the default commission rate comes from P-11. Personnel details (full name, date of birth, specialty, years of experience, hire date, commission rate, employment status) are view-only for the staff member and changed by the Manager (CBR-108). The employee code never changes (DBR-09). Only the Admin changes a position (CBR-109), and only when no unfinished work remains in the old position (CBR-87); changes to or from Admin follow BR-08, and the last active Admin cannot be demoted or set to Resigned (BR-07). |
| Status / lifecycle | Active (stored as Working) · Inactive (stored as Resigned, with Deleted At and a reason of 5–500 characters): every session of the account is signed out; the account stays Active if the Person still has a non-Inactive role, otherwise it becomes Inactive (CBR-86); phone and email are released only when every role is Inactive (DBR-28). |

**Entity: Package**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | The catalog of purchasable offerings — memberships, day passes, personal-training packages and single PT sessions — that orders are created from. |
| Key business attributes | Package name, description (≤ 500 characters), benefits (≤ 1000 characters, at most 10 lines of 3–100 characters, one benefit per line, DBR-15), package type, duration unit (Day / Month) and duration unit (Day / Month) and duration value: Day Pass \= 1 Day; Membership \= months from P-04; PT Single / PT Couple \= months from P-21; Single Session has no duration. End dates are computed by calendar month, never as 30 days (DBR-19, GBR-03). |
| Business identity | Five package types: Membership, Day Pass, PT Single, PT Couple and Single Session; stored values Membership, DayPass, PTSingle, PTCouple, SingleSession (GBR-01). Duration: Day Pass \= 1 Day; Membership \= months from P-04; PT Single / PT Couple \= months from P-21; Single Session has no duration. End dates are computed by calendar month, never as 30 days (DBR-19, GBR-03). Estimated session count is mandatory for PT types and empty for every other type. A single drop-in PT session is modeled as its own package type rather than a standalone price, so every training session always traces back through a Subscription. PT packages are sold by term, not by number of sessions: the session count here is only an approximation, and the real count is fixed on the order when it is paid (DBR-53). The name is 3–100 characters and unique among active packages (DBR-11). Prices include VAT, and a catalogue change never applies to existing orders (CBR-09). |
| Status / lifecycle | Active vs Inactive via Is Active flag; an Inactive package is no longer sold, but retired packages stay on file for existing orders (CBR-97). |

**Entity: Voucher**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A discount code a customer can apply to an order, subject to usage limits and scope restrictions. |
| Key business attributes | Voucher code, discount type (Percent / Amount), discount value, start/end date, max usage (total), max usage per customer (empty \= unlimited), applies-to scope (MembershipAndDayPass — default / MembershipOnly), used count, minimum order value, is-active flag |
| Business identity | Voucher Code is unique (4–20 uppercase letters and digits) and cannot be edited after first use. An order can use at most one voucher, and the scope is either membership packages and day passes, or membership packages only — PT packages and single sessions never accept a voucher (CBR-76). Used Count increments when the voucher is applied and decrements when the order is cancelled, the voucher is removed or the code is changed (BR-43–BR-45); the database check Used Count ≤ Max Usage keeps the cap correct under simultaneous use (GBR-13). |
| Status / lifecycle | Active vs Inactive via Is Active flag; also bounded by Start Date/End Date (last day inclusive). A voucher used at least once can only be deactivated, never deleted (CBR-98). |

**Entity: Order**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A purchase record for one package, snapshotting the terms at time of purchase so later price or config changes never alter existing orders. |
| Key business attributes | Order Code (lookup code shown to customer & staff), holder customer (and partner for a couple package), package, voucher, package name/description/benefits/unit price snapshot, discount amount, VAT rate & amount snapshot, channel (Counter/Online), creating Receptionist and shift (Counter only), payment due time, created time, paid time, cancel type/time/reason |
| Business identity | Identified by a system-generated Order Code (DH-yyyy-nnnn). Total amount is never stored — always derived as Unit Price Snapshot minus Discount Amount; the VAT amount is the part of that total that is tax (total × VAT% ÷ (100 \+ VAT%)) and is stored at creation (DBR-57). Payment details live on Transaction, not here. The price of an existing order cannot be edited — a wrong order is cancelled and a new one created (CBR-10). A Counter order always has its creator and shift; an Online order has neither. An Online order copies the payment deadline (P-09) and uses it as the slot hold time (CBR-40). A Counter order has no payment deadline; its slot stays Held until the order is paid or cancelled, and the shift cannot close while it is Pending (CBR-78). |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending (awaiting payment) · Paid (payment completed) · Cancelled (final; cancel type PaymentTimeout or ReplacedByNewOrder for Online orders only, InvalidPayment, or CancelledByReceptionist for Counter orders only with a reason of at least 5 characters). Allowed moves: Pending → Paid, Pending → Cancelled, and Paid → Cancelled only for a counter order within its own open shift (CBR-11). |

**Entity: Transaction**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A single payment attempt against an order — kept separate from Order because one online order can involve several attempts (retry after failure or an expired link). |
| Key business attributes | Amount (snapshot of amount due at creation), payment method (Cash / Transfer / OnlineGateway), gateway reference, received by (Receptionist, required for a successful Cash or Transfer payment, CBR-77), status, failure reason, needs-refund flag, refunded time, refunded by (Manager), refund note, created time, expiry time, completed time |
| Business identity | An order has at most one Success transaction and at most one Pending transaction at a time, enforced by the database. A counter order generates one Success transaction immediately. The online payment link lasts 5 minutes and never beyond the order deadline. |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending · Success · Failed · Expired. A Failed or Expired transaction leaves the order Pending so the customer can pay again (CBR-69). A Success transaction on a Cancelled order, or with the wrong amount, is flagged as needing a refund outside the system (CBR-72). The Manager pays the refund outside the system and then marks the transaction refunded, recording the time, the Manager and an optional note; only a Success transaction flagged Needs Refund can be marked (BR-47). |

**Entity: Shift**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A receptionist's work shift, used to reconcile cash and transactions at open and close. |
| Key business attributes | Work date, shift type (Morning/Afternoon), opening and closing Receptionist, opened/closed time, expected cash (sum of successful cash transactions of the shift), counted cash, variance reason (required when counts mismatch) |
| Business identity | Every open day has exactly two shifts, generated automatically from the opening hours — one per (work date, shift type) (CBR-104). Tied to the Receptionist who opened it and the one who closed it. Every payment taken while the shift is open is recorded in it (CBR-105). Variance itself isn't stored — always Counted Cash minus Expected Cash. A shift cannot be closed while one of its counter orders is still Pending (CBR-78). |
| Status / lifecycle | NotOpened · Open · Closed |

**Entity: Subscription**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | The usable entitlement a customer holds once an order is paid — the record actually consumed by check-ins and training sessions. |
| Key business attributes | Subscription type, holder customer, PT in charge (PT Single, PT Couple and Single Session only), start date, end date, fixed start time (PT packages, CBR-43), generated session count, swaps used, max swaps snapshot (P-08 at sale, PT packages), freezes used, max freezes snapshot (P-01 at sale, memberships) |
| Business identity | Created when the Order is paid, at most one per order, and tied to the Order (and, through it, the Package) that created it. The end date is the last valid day (GBR-03). The generated session count is fixed when the order is paid (BR-40). Swaps used and freezes used count against the snapshots of P-08 and P-01 taken when the order was paid; later parameter changes do not apply (GBR-04). A couple PT package produces a single shared Subscription with one common quota; the partner is recorded on the Order. |
| Status / lifecycle | Status by type: Membership — Active, Frozen, Expired, Cancelled; Day Pass — Active, Used, Expired, Cancelled; PT Single / PT Couple — Active, Expired, Cancelled (CBR-55); Single Session — Active, Completed, Expired, Cancelled. Cancelled means the underlying order was cancelled. Day passes and single sessions have Start Date \= End Date. |

**Entity: FreezeRecord**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A single freeze (temporary pause) applied to a customer's membership subscription. |
| Key business attributes | Start date, planned end date, actual end date, reason (5–500 characters) |
| Business identity | Always tied to exactly one subscription being frozen and one receptionist who processed it. No independent identity of its own. The planned end cannot be later than the maximum freeze length (P-02, default 1 month) or the days remaining on the package, and the number of freezes per package is capped by P-01 (default 1). Freezing is free (P-03). Cancelling a freeze early still counts as a freeze used. Both Start Date and End Date are frozen days; days frozen \= Actual End Date − Start Date \+ 1, added to the subscription end date (DBR-51). A subscription has at most one freeze in progress. When cancelled early, Actual End Date is earlier than Planned End Date but never earlier than Start Date. Open issue: how to record a freeze cancelled before its start date. |
| Status / lifecycle | No stored status field — inferred as in-progress when Actual End Date is null, completed once it's set. In progress (actual end date not yet set) · Completed (actual end date recorded). No delete — kept permanently for history. |

**Entity: CheckIn**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A single gym-entry record created each time a customer checks in. |
| Key business attributes | Check-in time, photo verified (yes/no) |
| Business identity | Tied to exactly one subscription (only Membership or Day Pass subscriptions can produce a check-in) and one receptionist who verified it. A membership allows unlimited check-ins within its validity; a day pass gives exactly one entry and needs no photo, so Photo Verified is no for it (BR-30, CBR-36). |
| Status / lifecycle | No status — a one-time event, fixed once created, never edited or deleted. |

**Entity: CustomerDeletionRequest**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A request to delete a customer profile that still has a running package or unused PT sessions; it waits for Manager approval (CBR-16). A profile with nothing remaining is deleted immediately without a request, and the deletion is written to the audit log (BR-15). |
| Key business attributes | Reason (5–500 characters), status, reject reason (5–500 characters, Rejected only), requested time, reviewed time |
| Business identity | Tied to the customer, the Receptionist who filed it and the Manager who reviewed it; the reviewer must not be the same Person as the customer (CBR-115). A customer has at most one Pending request. |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending · Approved (by a Manager; the profile becomes Inactive) · Rejected (by a Manager, reject reason 5–500 characters; the profile is unchanged). Never deleted. |

**Entity: TimeSlot**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A time slot a personal trainer publishes as available for customers to book. |
| Key business attributes | Date, start time (15-minute grid), end time (start time \+ P-06 minutes, default 90), status, order currently holding the slot, hold expiry time |
| Business identity | Tied to the trainer who published it. A trainer cannot publish two slots with the same start time on one date, and published slots must not overlap (DBR-33). A slot belongs to one customer, or to one pair of customers for a couple package (DBR-32). The hold is placed by the Pending order that selected the slot and lasts until the Online order's payment deadline (CBR-40); a Counter order's hold has no expiry time and ends when the order is paid or cancelled. |
| Status / lifecycle | Free (available) · Held (a Pending order has selected it) · Booked (the order is Paid) · Withdrawn (the PT removed a Free slot; it is kept for history instead of being deleted, GBR-05). The slot returns to Free when the order is cancelled for any reason, or when its session is cancelled or becomes Missed (DBR-36, CBR-68). |

**Entity: Session**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A single training session a customer books against a trainer's time slot. |
| Key business attributes | Status, session value, commission amount, PT who teaches, attendance marked time, auto-closed flag, missed reason (NoCheckIn / NoMembership / MembershipFrozen / MarkedAbsent — required when Missed), cancel type (ByPt / ByCustomer / GymClosed / PackageExpired — required when Cancelled), cancel reason, cancelled time, cancelled by (account), refund agreed  |
| Business identity | Tied to the subscription it was generated from and the time slot it occupies. The customer is derived from the subscription (a couple package also has the partner on the order). The PT who teaches is stored on the session: it changes when the session is transferred, and the commission follows the new PT (BR-68). Session value \= (price − discount) ÷ sessions generated, fixed when the order is paid; commission \= the PT's rate × session value (DBR-58, DBR-59). Cancelled By is the account that pressed Cancel: required for ByPt and ByCustomer, empty for GymClosed and PackageExpired. A ByPt cancellation also requires a reason (≥ 5 characters) and Refund Agreed \= yes (BR-66). |
| Status / lifecycle | Scheduled (booked, upcoming) · Completed (customer attended; couple: at least one member) · Missed (no check-in, no valid membership package, membership frozen, or marked absent by the PT) · Cancelled (by the PT with a cash refund, by the customer, or by the system when the PT package expires or the gym is closed that day). Completed, Missed and Cancelled are final (DBR-38). |

**Entity: SessionMoveLog**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A record of every move of a session to another slot or PT. |
| Key business attributes | Move type (CustomerSwap / PtOnBehalfSwap / PtReschedule / PtTransfer), old and new time slot, old and new PT, requested by (account — the customer for CustomerSwap, otherwise the PT), reason, moved time |
| Business identity | Tied to one session; old and new slots differ; the PT changes only for PtTransfer. Only a Scheduled session that has not started can be moved. CustomerSwap targets only Saturday or Sunday slots (BR-75); PtOnBehalfSwap may target any weekday (BR-62). |
| Status / lifecycle | No status — append-only history. CustomerSwap and PtOnBehalfSwap count toward the package swap limit (max swaps snapshot, BR-73); PtReschedule and PtTransfer do not (BR-64, BR-65). |

**Entity: LeaveRequest**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A staff member's request for time off, subject to manager approval. |
| Key business attributes | Leave type (Annual/Sick/Unpaid), leave date, shift (Morning/Afternoon/FullDay), reason, reject reason, submitted date, reviewed date, reminder-sent time |
| Business identity | Tied to the staff member (PT or Receptionist) who submitted it and the manager who reviewed it; an auto-rejected request has no reviewer. It must be submitted before 15:00 the day before the leave (P-12), a PT cannot request leave while still having a Scheduled session that day (CBR-83), and approval cannot drop a shift below the minimum staffing (P-13, P-14). An employee has at most one non-rejected request per (leave date, shift). Open issue: whether the Manager submits leave requests (UC-15) is not decided yet. |
| Status / lifecycle | Pending (awaiting review) · Approved (granted by a manager) · Rejected (denied by a manager with a reason, or automatically with the reason 'Approval deadline passed' if not decided by 20:00 the day before the leave, P-20) |

**Entity: Facility**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A piece of equipment or an area in the gym that can be reported for maintenance. |
| Key business attributes | Facility name, category (Cardio / FreeWeights / Machines / Amenities), location, quantity |
| Business identity | Identified by system ID; the name, category and location are descriptive and not required to be unique. Quantity is at least 1\. A facility cannot be removed while it has a maintenance request that is not Closed (CBR-99). |
| Status / lifecycle | Available (in normal use) · UnderMaintenance (currently being fixed) · Retired (taken out of service — the result of deleting the item, kept for history, GBR-05). Approving a maintenance request sets it to UnderMaintenance unless the Manager opts out; closing the request returns it to Available when no other request is InProgress (CBR-101, CBR-102). |

**Entity: MaintenanceRequest**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A report that a facility needs repair, tracked from report through approval to close-out. |
| Key business attributes | Request code (BT-nnnn, system-generated, unique), priority (Urgent / Normal — default / Low), warning tag placed (yes/no), description (10–500 characters), set under maintenance (chosen by the Manager on approval, CBR-101), reject reason, acceptance note (entered when closing), reported time, reviewed time, closed time |
| Business identity | Identified by its Request Code. Tied to the facility being reported, the receptionist who reported it, the manager who reviewed it, and the receptionist who closed it. |
| Status / lifecycle | Open (just reported) · InProgress (approved by a manager) · Rejected (denied by a manager, with a reason) · Closed (receptionist confirms the fix, enters an acceptance note and closes it). Allowed moves: Open → InProgress → Closed, or Open → Rejected (DBR-46). |

**Entity: StaffAttendance**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A staff member's clock-in and clock-out record for one shift. Modeled for later use only — staff timekeeping is out of scope for this release (DBR-63). |
| Key business attributes | Work date, shift type (Morning/Afternoon), check-in time, check-in photo, check-out time, status, note |
| Business identity | Tied to the employee. At most one record per (employee, work date, shift type), and check-out must be later than check-in. Kept separate from CheckIn because a member's check-in belongs to a subscription while staff attendance belongs to a shift. The photo only verifies staff attendance and is never used for member check-in. |
| Status / lifecycle | Present · Late · Absent · OnLeave |

**Entity: PrivateNote**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A PT's private note about a specific client, visible and editable only by the PT who wrote it. |
| Key business attributes | Content (1–2000 characters), last updated date, deleted date |
| Business identity | At most one active PrivateNote per (PT, Customer) combination; a deleted note does not count, so a new one can be written afterwards (DBR-61). The note stays invisible to any other PT, even after the customer moves to another PT (CBR-92). |
| Status / lifecycle | Active · Deleted (soft delete — hidden permanently). The PT can edit an active note at any time; saving overwrites it (BR-58, BR-59). |

**Entity: TrainingPlan**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A workout or meal plan authored by a PT for a specific client. |
| Key business attributes | Plan type (Workout / Meal), draft title, draft content (≤ 10 000 characters), published title, published content, published time (empty \= never published), created time, last updated time, deleted time. |
| Business identity | At most one active plan per (PT, Customer, Plan Type) combination; a deleted plan does not count (DBR-62). The PT can edit or delete their own plans at any time (BR-60, BR-61). |
| Status / lifecycle | Never published (Published At empty, client sees nothing) → Published. Publishing copies the draft into Published Title / Content and sets Published At; the client always reads the published copy, so editing the draft changes nothing for the client until the PT publishes again (BR-60). Deleted (soft delete) plans disappear from My Plan immediately (BR-61). |

**Entity: Feedback**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A message submitted by a Customer through the suggestion box — the system's sole feedback channel. |
| Key business attributes | Content (10–1000 characters), submitted date, read date, read by (Manager) |
| Business identity | No natural unique key; identified by system ID. Only the Manager can read feedback (CBR-106); there is no reply or resolution workflow (CBR-107). |
| Status / lifecycle | Unread → Read (one-way) |

**Entity: BlogPost**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Public marketing content published by Manager for visitors and customers to read. |
| Key business attributes | Title, category (Training/Nutrition/News), excerpt, content, cover image, published date |
| Business identity | No natural unique key stated; titles are not required to be unique. Written by a Manager. |
| Status / lifecycle | Inactive (not shown on the public site — a new post or one taken down) · Active (published; requires a published date). Switching to Inactive removes the post from the public site immediately (CBR-100). |

**Entity: Notification**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A broadcast message sent by Manager — or automatically by the system — to a defined audience. |
| Key business attributes | Title (5–100 characters), content (10–500 characters), audience (AllCustomers / ActiveMembers / PTs / Receptionists / AllStaff / Individual), scheduled time (empty \= send now), sent time (empty \= not sent yet), created time, sender (empty only for system notifications, which always target Individual) |
| Business identity | No natural unique key; identified by system ID. |
| Status / lifecycle | Scheduled (Sent At empty, waiting for Scheduled At) → Sent (Sent At set; recipients created). No further change after sending. |

**Entity: NotificationRecipient**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Tracks whether a specific Account has read a specific Notification; resolves the many-to-many relationship between them. |
| Key business attributes | Read date |
| Business identity | Unique per (Notification, Account) combination. Only people with an account receive in-app notifications; dependants are informed outside the system (GBR-15). |
| Status / lifecycle | Unread → Read (Read At null vs set) |

**Entity: SystemConfig**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | A key-value store of the adjustable business parameters P-01…P-21 (e.g., freeze limits, VAT %, default commission %, PT package durations)."  |
| Key business attributes | Config key, config value, description, last updated time, updated by |
| Business identity | Config Key is unique across the system. A change applies only to records created afterwards (GBR-04). |
| Status / lifecycle | N/A |

**Entity: OperatingHourException**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Overrides the default operating hours for one specific date (e.g., Tet, public holidays). |
| Key business attributes | Apply date, open time, close time, closed-all-day flag, note, set by (Manager) |
| Business identity | Apply Date is unique — at most one exception entry per date. No PT session is generated on a day declared closed (CBR-56). |
| Status / lifecycle | N/A |

**Entity: AuditLog**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | An immutable record of every sensitive action performed in the system, for traceability. |
| Key business attributes | Acting account (empty when a system job acted), acting role (Admin / Manager / PT / Receptionist / Customer — the role the user was working in; empty for jobs), action, entity name, entity ID, field changed, old value, new value, reason, created time |
| Business identity | No natural unique key; identified by system ID. Only the Admin can read it (CBR-103). Passwords and verification codes are never written to it (CBR-112, DBR-02). |
| Status / lifecycle | N/A — records are append-only, never updated or deleted |

\[Rules about data that are not obvious from the ERD. \]

| DBR-02 | Password  | Masked, 8–64 characters, at least one letter and one digit, different from the current password; stored hashed and never displayed or logged. **(Length proposed by our team, to be confirmed.)**  | Account  |
| DBR-03 | Verification code  | Exactly 6 digits, single use.  | Account |
| DBR-04 | Date of birth  | Not in the future; age ≤ 100\.  | Customer, Employee  |

| DBR-16 | Event timestamps  | Business event times (paid, cancelled, checked in, reviewed, closed…) are written when the event happens and never edited.  | All entities  |

End dates are computed by calendar month (GBR-03), never as 30 days. | UC-10, UC-20, UC-21, UC-22  |

Every Person has a phone number except a Dependent profile (DBR-24), because the phone number is what the Receptionist and the Admin use to find an existing Person (CBR-19, CBR-114).  | UC-05, UC-07, UC-16, UC-IDENT   |

When every role of the Person is Inactive, the phone number and email are released immediately and the person can get a new profile without waiting (CBR-23).  | UC-05, UC-07, UC-13, UC-16  |

| DBR-31 | Customer (walk-in)  | A walk-in customer still needs a profile containing at least full name and phone number.  | UC-16, UC-20  |

#### ***3.3.3  States and Transitions***

### 

| ID | Data  | Rule Description | Applies to / Use Cases |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| DBR-34 | Customer.Status  | A customer profile has exactly five states: New, Active, Frozen, Expired, Inactive.  | UC-16, UC-19, UC-41   |
| DBR-35  | Customer.Status  | Inactive is a final state; an Inactive profile never returns to any other state.  | UC-16 |
| DBR-36 | TimeSlot.Status  | A PT slot has three states: Free, Held and Booked. When the customer or Receptionist selects a slot and the system creates a Pending order, the slot becomes Held at that moment and nobody else can select it. When the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked. When the order is Cancelled for any reason (CBR-70, CBR-71, CBR-72, CBR-11) the slot returns to Free. A Free slot that the PT removes becomes Withdrawn and is kept for history (GBR-05). A slot held by a Counter order has no hold expiry; it stays Held until the order is paid or cancelled. | UC-21, UC-37, UC-PAY  |
| DBR-37 | Session.Status  | A session has four states: Scheduled, Completed, Missed, Cancelled.  | UC-31, UC-32, UC-35, UC-36  |
| DBR-38 | Session.Status  | A session in a final state (Completed, Missed, Cancelled) cannot be changed by anyone.  | UC-31, UC-32  |
| DBR-39 | Order.Status | An order has three states: Pending, Paid, Cancelled. There is no refunded state — all refunds are handled outside the system.  | UC-20, UC-21, UC-22, UC-24, UC-25, UC-26, UC-PAY  |
| DBR-40 | Order.Status  | An order moves only along Pending → Paid, Pending → Cancelled, and Paid → Cancelled (only under CBR-11). Cancelled is final.  | UC-20, UC-21, UC-22, UC-PAY  |
| DBR-41 | Transaction.Status  | Every payment attempt for an order is recorded as a transaction with four states: Pending, Success, Failed, Expired. One order may have several transactions.  | UC-20, UC-21, UC-22, UC-24, UC-25, UC-26, UC-37, UC-PAY  |
| DBR-42 | Transaction  | An order has at most one Success transaction and at most one Pending transaction at any time. A Paid order gets no further transactions.  | UC-PAY  |
| DBR-43 | Order.Cancel Type  | A cancelled order records its cancellation type: payment deadline passed (CBR-70), replaced by a new order (CBR-71), invalid payment (CBR-72) or cancelled by the Receptionist (CBR-11).  | UC-20, UC-24, UC-25, UC-26  |
| DBR-44 | LeaveRequest.Status  | A leave request has three states: Pending, Approved, Rejected.  | UC-14, UC-15  |
| DBR-45 | MaintenanceRequest.Status  | A maintenance request has four states: Open, In Progress, Rejected, Closed.  | UC-28, UC-29  |
| DBR-46 | MaintenanceRequest.Status  | A maintenance request moves only along Open → In Progress → Closed, or Open → Rejected. No step is skipped. | UC-28, UC-29  |

## **4\. User Requirements** {#4.-user-requirements}

### **4.1 Actors** {#4.1-actors}

\[An actor is someone/something that interacts with the system. 

* The only external entities that interact with the system  
* ﻿Actors are outside the system and not part of it  
* ﻿A user is an individual, whereas an actor represents the role played by all users of the same type  
* There are other types of actors in addition to or in place of human actors: external systems, I/O devices, or timers

Following are some questions you might ask to help user representatives identify actors

* Who (or what) is notified when something occurs within the system?  
* Who (or what) provides information or services to the system?  
* Who (or what) helps the system respond to and complete a task?

This part gives the description of system actors, you can follow the table form as below\]

| \# | Actor | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | System User | Abstract actor, parent of every actor that holds a login account (Customer, PT, Receptionist, Manager, Admin). Exists so that Log In, Log Out, Password Recovery, and Manage Personal Account are defined once instead of once per role. Guest does not inherit from this actor, since Guest has no account yet — Guest reaches Customer only through registration (UC-05), which is modeled as a note, not a generalization arrow.  |
| 2 | Guest | A person who does not yet have an account. Browses public content (services, pricing, blog) and registers an account. Becomes a Customer once the account is active. Not a specialisation of Customer — the two actors share no use case.  |
| 3 | Customer  | A person who has an account with the gym. Buys packages online, books, reschedules, or cancels PT sessions, tracks their own schedule, membership status and transaction history, views training and meal plans, and submits feedbacks.  |
| 4 | Staff  | Abstract actor, parent of PT and Receptionist. Exists so that leave-request submission is defined once for both roles. Never assigned a use case other than Submit Leave Request.  |
| 5 | PT (Personal Trainer)  | Publishes availability for any future date (no weekly/monthly limit), marks no-show sessions when a customer does not attend, reschedules, reassigns, or cancels a session they can't teach, tracks their teaching schedule and assigned clients, writes private notes on clients, and drafts training and meal plans. Inherits from Staff. |
| 6 | Receptionist  | Front-desk operator. Manages customer profiles and creates customer login accounts, sells packages at the counter, collects payment, checks customers in, reports and closes facility maintenance requests once confirmed fixed, freezes memberships, and reconciles cash at shift close.  |
| 7 | Manager  | Runs the gym. Configures system parameters, operating hours, the service package catalogue and vouchers; maintains personnel details of existing staff (full name, date of birth, specialty, experience, hire date, commission rate, resignation) but never creates staff accounts or changes a position; manages the facility catalogue and blog posts; approves or rejects customer deletion requests, leave requests and maintenance requests; views system-wide transactions and records refunds made outside the system for invalid online payments; is the only role that reads customer feedback; sends notifications; views the aggregated dashboard (without audit data). A Manager may not approve the deletion of their own customer profile   |
| 8 | Admin  | System administrator. Creates and manages all internal accounts (Admin, Manager, PT, Receptionist), views the audit log, and views operational reports with audit metrics. Does not create customer accounts.  |
| 9 | Payment Gateway (VNPay)  | External system. Receives online payment requests for self-service membership purchases (UC-22) and self-service single PT session bookings (UC-37), and returns the payment result. Not used when a PT single/couple package is sold at the counter (UC-21) — those are always paid in cash or bank transfer.  |
| 10 | Email / OTP Service  | External system. Delivers one-time email verification codes for account registration, password recovery, and profile claiming. Not used for sign-in — login is email/phone plus password only, no OTP.  |

### **4.2 Use Cases (UC)** {#4.2-use-cases-(uc)}

\[A use case (UC) describes a sequence of interactions between a system and an external actor that results in the actor being able to achieve some outcome of value. The names of use cases are always written in the form of a verb followed by an object. Select strong, descriptive names to make it evident from the name that the use case will deliver something valuable for some user.

Following are some questions you might ask to help user representatives identify use cases

* What will the actor use the system for?  
* Will the actor create, store, change, remove, or read data in the system?  
* Will the actor need to inform the system about external events or changes?  
* Will the actor need to be informed about certain occurrences in the system?

This part describes the use cases you could define, you can follow the table form as below\]

| ID | Use Case | Feature | Use Case Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
|     UC-01 | Login | System User | Authenticate with an email address or phone number plus a password; either identifies exactly one account. If the account serves more than one role that is not Inactive, the user selects the working role (staff position or Customer) on the Select Role screen before any home screen opens; an account with a single role goes straight to that role's home screen. An account created at the counter that has no password yet cannot sign in and is pointed to Forgot Password. An account that serves only the Customer role is locked for 5 minutes after 5 consecutive wrong passwords (P-17, P-18); an account that serves any staff role is never locked automatically.  |
|     UC-02 | Logout  | System User  | End the current session and securely sign out.  |
|     UC-03 | Recover Password  | System User, Email Gateway | Reset a forgotten password via a time-limited verification code sent to the registered email; all active sessions are invalidated after a successful reset. The same flow is used to set the first password of an account created by the Receptionist at the counter. |
| UC-04 | Manage Personal Account   | System User  | View one's own profile and keep sign-in details current, in any role. Customers and staff may change only their avatar, email, phone number and password. A new email is verified by a code sent to the new email; a new phone number is verified by a code sent to the account's current email; the new value is checked for duplicates before the code is sent and again when saved. After an email change the old email is notified and every other session is signed out. Customer name, date of birth, check-in photo and guardian details are changed only by the Receptionist; staff personnel details are changed by the Manager; position and account status are changed only by the Admin. The Dependent profiles tab is shown only in the Customer role, and the account menu offers Switch Role when the account serves more than one role.  |
| UC-05 | Register Account  | Guest | Self-register as a new customer directly on the website; phone/email uniqueness is validated against existing records |
| UC-Claim | Claim An Existing Profile Via Verification Code  | Guest  | Link a walk-in profile already created by the Receptionist to a new self-service login using a verification code sent to the email on file, so no duplicate customer record is created. If the email supplied does not match, the guest is told the profile is registered under a different address; if the profile already has a login, the guest is routed to password recovery; if the profile holds no email address, the guest is asked to complete the claim at the counter.  |
| UC-IDENT | Check Phone/Email Duplication & Identify Profile  |  | Detect whether a phone/email already exists in the system and route Register/Claim flows accordingly — invoked by UC-05.  |
| UC-06 | Explore Services & Pricing  | Guest  | Browse packages, pricing, and blog content publicly before signing up.  |
| UC-07 | Manage System Accounts  | Admin | Create staff accounts and their employee records for every position (Admin, Manager, PT, Receptionist); if the phone number matches an active Person, check an identity document and attach the staff role to that Person, reusing the existing account. Change an employee's position (only when no unfinished work remains; only the Admin can create or promote an Admin). Lock or unlock an account with a reason of 5–500 characters, including early unlock of a temporarily locked customer account. An account becomes Inactive only automatically, when every role of its Person is Inactive. The last active Admin cannot be deleted, locked, demoted or set to Resigned. Customer accounts are never created here; passwords are reset only by the owner through Forgot Password.  |
| UC-08 | View Audit Log  | Admin | Review a chronological, field-level log of data-changing actions for traceability. |
| UC-09 | Configure System Parameters  | Manager | Set system parameters — financial (VAT, default PT commission %) and operational (freeze limit and duration, minimum shift staffing, leave submission cut-off and leave approval cut-off, attendance window, swap limit, online payment deadline, and so on). Price and parameter changes never apply retroactively to existing orders.  |
| UC-10 | Manage Service Package Catalog  | Manager | Create, update, publish and retire the packages the gym sells — gym membership packages, day passes and PT packages (single and couple) — each with its name, duration or session count, price and sale status. Retiring a package only stops new sales; packages already purchased keep the terms captured at the time of purchase. |
| UC-11 | Configure Operating Hours  | Manager | Define a default daily operating schedule, with the ability to configure exceptions for specific dates. Every open day is split automatically into a morning and an afternoon shift — there is no manual rostering. Operating hours are used to validate bookings, check-ins and PT time-slot declarations.  |
| UC-12 | Manage Vouchers  | Manager | Create and maintain discount vouchers: code, discount value, validity period, total usage cap, per-customer usage limit, minimum order value, and the package types the voucher may be applied to. PT packages are outside every voucher's scope. A voucher can be deactivated; codes already applied to an order keep the terms captured at that time.  |
| UC-13 | Manage Personnel Records  | Manager | Maintain the personnel details of existing staff: full name, date of birth, specialty, years of experience, hire date, PT commission rate and employment status. Staff accounts are created and positions are changed only by the Admin (UC-07); email and phone number are changed by the staff member in UC-04. Recording a resignation (reason required) sets the employee to Resigned, signs out every session of the account and keeps the account Active only if the Person still has another role that is not Inactive. |
| UC-14 | Submit Leave Request  | Staff | Request time off. A request must be submitted before the submission cut-off on the day immediately preceding the leave date (configurable, 15:00 by default); unexpected absences are handled directly with the Manager outside the system. For a PT, submission is blocked if a teaching session is already scheduled within the requested period. Final approval is also subject to the minimum on-duty headcount for the affected shift. |
| UC-15 | Process Staff Leave Requests  | Manager  | Approve or reject leave requests. Approval is blocked if it would breach minimum shift staffing, and a rejection requires a reason. If the Manager takes no action by the approval cut-off on the day immediately preceding the leave date (configurable, 20:00 by default), the request is rejected automatically.  |
| UC-16 | Manage Customer Profiles  | Receptionist  | Create, look up and update customer profiles at the counter, including walk-in and dependent profiles, and capture the check-in photo used to verify entry. The phone number and email are checked for duplicates before a profile is created. Every deletion request needs a reason: a profile with no active package and no unused quota is removed straight away, otherwise the request is sent to the Manager for approval.  |
| UC-17 | Process Customer Deletion Requests  | Manager | Approve/reject pending deletion requests for members with an active package/unused quota, reviewing the reason submitted by Receptionist.  |
| UC-18 | Freeze A Membership Package  | Receptionist  | Pause an active membership package (never a PT package or expired package) free of charge, within the freeze count and length limits (P-01, P-02). A freeze is never blocked by PT sessions: before saving, the system lists every Scheduled session inside the freeze period, and on saving they become Missed (reason: membership frozen). The package resumes automatically at the end of the freeze; the Receptionist may also end it early, and the end date moves out only by the days actually frozen. A Receptionist cannot freeze their own package  |
| UC-19 | Check A Customer In At The Gym  | Receptionist  | Look up a customer's profile by customer code or phone number and manually record their check-in; verify the customer against the check-in photo; entry is granted only if the customer has a valid gym membership package or day pass — a PT-only package does not grant gym access.  |
| UC-20 | Create Order & Collect Payment At Counter  | Receptionist  | Record an in-person purchase (including day pass) for a new or existing customer and collect cash or bank transfer (confirmed only after the money is received); price, VAT and discount are snapshotted. A wrong paid order can be cancelled only within the same shift, with a reason, and refunded at the counter.   |
| UC-21 | Sell A PT Package  | Receptionist  | Process the sale of a single or couple PT package. The customer must hold a valid gym membership (both members for a couple package), and customers under 10 cannot buy either type. The customer chooses the PT, and the Receptionist sets a fixed weekly schedule matching the PT's declared slots; the initial fixed schedule falls on weekdays only, with weekends shown but not selectable. Payment is by cash or bank transfer only. The package is sold by term: the Receptionist picks the start date, the end date is start date plus the package duration (last day inclusive), and one session is generated for every Monday-to-Friday in the term at the fixed slot; the number of sessions is fixed when the order is Paid. An employee who also trains as a customer must choose a different PT, and the Receptionist cannot sell to their own customer profile.. Alternatively, for a walk-in customer without an account, the Receptionist can sell a single session for today only, checked against the customer's day pass or gym membership for that day and against age (under 10 not allowed), with payment taken immediately.  |
| UC-22 | Purchase A Package Via Self-Service  | Customer, VNPay | Buy a gym membership package online through a payment gateway without visiting the counter; not applicable to PT packages, which sell only through Receptionist. A failed or expired payment can be retried until the order's payment deadline; after that the order is cancelled and a new order is needed.  |
| UC-23 | Apply A Voucher To An Order  | Customer, Receptionist  | Apply a discount voucher to an order — one voucher per order. Validity is checked when the code is applied: validity period, total usage, per-customer limit, minimum order value measured on the price before discount, and whether the order's package type falls inside the voucher's scope. PT packages never accept a voucher. Usage is counted on apply and returned if the voucher is removed or the order is cancelled; the voucher cannot be changed while a payment is pending.  |
| UC-PAY | Process Payment & Record Transaction  | VNPay  | Record each payment attempt as a transaction. Counter payments (cash/transfer) succeed immediately; online payments go through the gateway — success marks the order Paid and grants the package, failure or expiry keeps the order pending for retry. A success received for a cancelled or mismatched order is flagged for manual refund.  |
| UC-24 | Look Up Personal Transaction History  | Customer | View one's own past orders and payments.  |
| UC-25 | Open Shift, Reconcile Transactions & Close Shift  | Receptionist | Open the shift, view transactions recorded in it, cancel a wrong order if needed, then compare expected cash from successful cash transactions with cash on hand; any discrepancy requires a reason before closing. The shift cannot be closed while any counter order from that shift is still Pending — each must be paid or cancelled first.  |
| UC-26 | Look Up System-Wide Transaction History  | Manager | View all transactions across the gym for oversight; filter by payment method and list successful payments that need a manual refund.  |
| UC-27 | Manage Facility/Equipment Catalog  | Manager | Maintain the register of facilities and equipment — name, category, location or area, quantity and current condition. The register is what the Receptionist selects from when reporting a fault, and retired items stop appearing in new maintenance requests. |
| UC-28 | Create Facility Maintenance Request  | Receptionist | Report a facility/equipment issue that needs repair, initiating an approval workflow only Manager can advance  |
| UC-29 | Process Facility Maintenance Requests  | Manager | Review and approve/reject facility maintenance requests submitted by Receptionist; approved requests move to In Progress and are closed by Receptionist once resolved.  |
| UC-30 | Declare Available Time Slots | PT | Set 90-minute time slots available to teach, including weekends (required to support weekend-only session swaps). Declared slots may not overlap, no buffer time is required between consecutive sessions, they must fall within the configured operating hours, and they may be published for any future date without limit.  |
| UC-31 | Mark Session No-Show  | PT | Record attendance for a scheduled session, including marking a client absent, which deducts the quota with no refund. Attendance can be recorded from the session start until 24 hours after it ends. For a couple package, absence is recorded only when both members are absent. If nothing is marked, the session closes automatically: Completed if the customer checked in that day, otherwise Missed. A session falling on a day when the customer no longer holds a valid gym membership does not take place and closes as Missed.   |
| UC-32 | Track Teaching Schedule & Assigned Clients  | PT | View upcoming sessions and the list of assigned clients on a dashboard. Sessions created via a Receptionist-sold PT package appear here automatically once paid, without requiring PT confirmation.  |
| UC-33 | Write Private Notes On Clients  | PT | Record notes about a client, visible and editable only by the PT who wrote them.  |
| UC-34 | Draft Training Plans & Meal Plans  | PT | Create/update a workout & diet plan attached to a client's profile, visible to the client once published.  |
| UC-35 | Handle A Session The PT Cannot Teach  | PT | After arranging matters directly with the customer, the PT resolves a scheduled session they cannot teach. Only the PT in charge can act, and only while the session is still Scheduled and has not started. There are three options: reschedule to another free slot of the same PT within the PT package term (never after its end date); transfer to another PT the customer has chosen, in which case the commission goes to the new PT; or cancel, which requires a reason and confirmation that the customer agreed to be repaid in cash by the PT outside the system. A cancelled session is still deducted from the package quota and the original PT still earns the commission. The session value never changes and no refund transaction is created. A rescheduled or transferred session must fall on a date the customer still holds a valid gym membership. The customer is notified automatically (both members for a couple package), and the new PT is notified on transfer. The same screen offers 'Swap on behalf of the customer' for a customer without an account (BR-62), logged as PtOnBehalfSwap and counted toward the swap limit.  |
| UC-36 | Track Personal Training Schedule  | Customer | View upcoming and past PT sessions.  |
| UC-37 | Book A Single Session With A PT | Customer | Reserve a one-off, per-session training slot with a chosen PT. The date must fall within the customer's valid membership package period, or be the current day if the customer instead holds a valid day pass. Selectable slots are limited to the current week, with the following week opening from Saturday onward. The slot becomes Held as soon as the Pending order is created and stays Held until the order's payment deadline; it becomes Booked when the order is Paid and returns to Free if the order is cancelled. Payment is made only through the online gateway. |
| UC-38 | Reschedule A Session In A PT Package  | Customer | Swap a package session's date and time to a weekend slot the PT has declared free, selectable only within the current week, with the following week opening from Saturday onward, and only to a date the customer still holds a valid gym package. A package allows up to 3 swaps in total. For a couple package, either member may perform the swap. Where the customer has no self-service account, the PT performs the swap on their behalf, and it counts toward the same limit of 3\.  |
| UC-39 | Cancel A Booked Session  | Customer | Cancel a previously booked session at any time; always deducted from quota with no refund, with a warning shown before confirming.  |
| UC-40 | View Training Plan & Meal Plan From PT | Customer | View the workout/diet plan authored by the assigned PT  |
| UC-41 | Track Membership & Package Status  | Customer | Check status (Active/Frozen/Expired) and remaining quota of owned packages; Frozen/Expired status blocks check-in and new PT bookings.  |
| UC-42 | Submit Feedback  | Customer | Send feedback via the suggestion box — the sole feedback channel in the system, visible only to Manager  |
| UC-43 | View Customer Feedback  | Manager | Review feedback submitted by customers through the sole feedback channel in the system.  |
| UC-44 | Send Notifications  | Manager | Broadcast text-only notifications to customers or staff.  |
| UC-45 | Manage Blog Posts  | Manager | Write, edit, publish and unpublish the blog articles shown on the public site. Published posts appear on the public pages browsed by guests; unpublishing removes a post from the public site without deleting it.  |
| UC-46 | View Aggregated Dashboard  | Manager | View a single consolidated operational report; the query range is not limited, reflecting a snapshot at query time.  |
| UC-47 | View Operational Reports & Audit Metrics  | Admin | View system-wide operational reports plus additional audit-related metrics not visible to the Manager.  |
