## **13\. Background Job Inventory** {#13.-background-job-inventory}

### **13.0 Common behavior for all jobs** {#13.0-common-behavior-for-all-jobs}

All times use the Asia/Ho\_Chi\_Minh time zone (UTC+7). Daily jobs run in sequence at 00:05: JOB-01 → 02 → 03 → 04\. JOB-01 runs before JOB-02 because the frozen days must be added before expiry is evaluated. JOB-05, JOB-06 and JOB-07 each run every minute, independently of each other.

Each run selects records by state, not by "yesterday", so a failed or late run is caught up by the next run.

Each record is processed in its own transaction and its state is re-checked just before writing. One failing record does not block the others.

Jobs do not overlap: a per-minute job starts its next run only 1 minute after the previous run has finished.

Every state change is written to the AuditLog with the actor \= System.

Database unreachable:

+ Daily jobs retry 3 times at 5-minute intervals, then log a critical error and wait for the next scheduled run.  
+ Per-minute jobs do not retry separately; the next run one minute later is the retry.

### **13.1 Resume Expired Membership Freezes (JOB-01)** {#13.1-resume-expired-membership-freezes-(job-01)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily at 00:05, first job of the daily chain

**Purpose:** Automatically reopens a membership package whose freeze period has ended, without any Receptionist action, and adds the frozen days to the package's expiry date.

**Related:** UC-18, UC-19, UC-41 · Rules BR-25, BR-26, DBR-51, DBR-13

Processing steps:

1\. Find freezes still in progress (ActualEndDate is NULL) whose PlannedEndDate is before today; the Planned End Date itself is still a frozen day.

2\. Set ActualEndDate \= PlannedEndDate. A late run does not change the dates: the package End Date is extended exactly as if the job had run on time.

3\. Change the subscription Status Frozen → Active; change Customers.Status Frozen → Active only if the profile is still Frozen (an Inactive profile is never changed — DBR-35).

4\. Add the number of days actually frozen, ActualEndDate − StartDate \+ 1 (both ends are frozen days), to the subscription End Date (DBR-51).

5\. Log the number of packages resumed.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | Retries up to 3 times at 5-minute intervals. If it still fails, logs a critical error and waits for the next daily run. Packages remain Frozen until the next successful run; because ActualEndDate \= PlannedEndDate, the customer loses no days. |
| Error while processing one freeze | Rolls back that package only and logs a warning. Other packages are still processed. The failed package is processed again in the next run. |
| No freezes due | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.2 Expire Membership and PT Packages (JOB-02)** {#13.2-expire-membership-and-pt-packages-(job-02)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily, right after JOB-01

**Purpose:** A membership package past its expiry date no longer grants gym access; a member left with no valid package becomes Expired. A PT package past its expiry date becomes Expired and its unused sessions are cancelled.

**Related:** UC-19, UC-21, UC-22, UC-41 · Rules GBR-03, GBR-14, DBR-34, DBR-48, DBR-52, CBR-55

Processing steps:

1\. Find Active membership packages whose End Date is before today. The End Date is the last day the package is valid, so a package only loses validity from the following day.

2\. Change Subscriptions.Status Active → Expired for SubscriptionType \= Membership only (day passes are handled by JOB-03, PT packages by step 5).

3\. For each Active member who lost a package: if no membership package or day pass is still valid, change the profile Active → Expired. Frozen members are left unchanged.

4\. A membership package or day pass is valid when its Status is Active and its End Date is today or later (including a package whose Start Date is in the future — DBR-52). A PT package or single session never counts (DBR-48).

5\. Find PTSingle and PTCouple subscriptions still Active whose End Date is before today and change them to Expired (CBR-55).

6\. For each such package, every session still Scheduled whose date is after the package End Date becomes Cancelled with CancelType \= PackageExpired, CancelledAt \= now, CancelledByAccountId \= NULL, no refund and no term extension; its time slot returns to Free. Sessions dated on or before the End Date are left to JOB-04.

7\. Log the number of membership packages, PT packages and members changed and sessions cancelled.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | Retries up to 3 times at 5-minute intervals. If it still fails, logs a critical error and waits for the next daily run. Expired packages remain Active until the next successful run. |
| Error while processing one package or member | Rolls back that record only and logs a warning. Other records are still processed. The failed record is processed again in the next run. |
| No packages expired | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.3 Expire Unused Day Passes (JOB-03)** {#13.3-expire-unused-day-passes-(job-03)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily, right after JOB-02

**Purpose:** A day pass grants a single entry on its valid day; if it is not used by the end of that day, it becomes invalid.

**Related:** UC-19, UC-20 · Rules BR-29, BR-32, CBR-36, DBR-48

Processing steps:

1\. Find subscriptions with SubscriptionType \= DayPass, Status \= Active and End Date (= Start Date) before today. A pass used at check-in is already Used (BR-29), so it is outside the scan.

2\. Change those passes to Expired.

3\. For each Active member who lost a pass: if no membership package or day pass is still valid, change the profile Active → Expired. Frozen members are left unchanged.

4\. Log the number of passes expired.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | Retries up to 3 times at 5-minute intervals. If it still fails, logs a critical error and waits for the next daily run. Day passes remain Active until the next successful run. |
| Error while processing one pass or member | Rolls back that record only and logs a warning. Other records are still processed. The failed record is processed again in the next run. |
| No day passes to process | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.4 Auto-Close Unmarked PT Sessions (JOB-04)** {#13.4-auto-close-unmarked-pt-sessions-(job-04)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily, right after JOB-03

**Purpose:** Finalizes PT sessions the trainer did not mark within the allowed period, so session quota and commission can be closed. The trainer can still mark attendance earlier (UC-31); this job only handles sessions still Scheduled after that period ends.

**Related:** UC-31, UC-32 · Rules BR-54, CBR-42, CBR-63, CBR-64, CBR-67, CBR-80, DBR-38

**Parameters:** Attendance window after a session ends — default 24 hours (P-07)

Processing steps:

1\. Find sessions still Scheduled whose end time plus the attendance window (P-07) is earlier than now. Because the job runs once a day, a session may stay Scheduled until the next daily run after the window has passed.

2\. For each session, evaluate in order and stop at the first match:

    a. The session belongs to a PT package (single or couple) and the customer has no valid membership package on the session date (couple package: neither member has one) → Status \= Missed, MissedReason \= NoMembership. A day pass does not replace a membership package.

    b. A check-in exists on the session date for any membership or day-pass subscription of the customer (couple package: of either member) → Status \= Completed.

    c. Otherwise → Status \= Missed, MissedReason \= NoCheckIn.

(Sessions inside a freeze are already Missed with MissedReason \= MembershipFrozen at freeze time — CBR-62 — and are not seen by this job.)

3\. Set IsAutoClosed \= 1 and AttendanceMarkedAt \= now. CommissionAmount is not recalculated: it was fixed when the order was Paid and belongs to the PT in Sessions.PtEmployeeId; a Missed session earns it like a Completed one (CBR-80).

4\. Log the number of sessions per outcome.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | Retries up to 3 times at 5-minute intervals. If it still fails, logs a critical error and waits for the next daily run. Sessions remain Scheduled until the next successful run. |
| Error while processing one session | Rolls back that session only and logs a warning. Other sessions are still processed. The session stays Scheduled and is processed again in the next run. |
| No sessions to close | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.5 Cancel Overdue Online Orders (JOB-05)** {#13.5-cancel-overdue-online-orders-(job-05)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every minute

**Purpose:** Cancels online orders not fully paid within the payment deadline and releases what they were holding. The order was never paid, so no package or session has been granted; the customer must create a new order, with price and voucher recalculated at that time.

**Related:** UC-22, UC-26, UC-37, UC-PAY · Rules CBR-70, CBR-40, CBR-53, DBR-36, DBR-43, BR-44, CBR-72

**Parameters:** Online order payment deadline (also the slot hold time) — default 20 minutes from order creation (P-09), copied onto the order (Orders.PaymentDueAt) when it is created

Processing steps:

1\. Find orders on the Online channel with status Pending, past the payment deadline recorded on the order, and with no successful transaction.

2\. For each order, inside one transaction: re-check that it is still Pending with no successful transaction, then set Orders.Status \= Cancelled, CancelType \= PaymentTimeout, CancelledAt \= now, CancelReason \= NULL.

3\. Change the order's Pending transactions to Expired.

4\. Every time slot held by the order (TimeSlots.HeldByOrderId \= the order) returns to Status \= Free with HeldByOrderId \= NULL and HoldExpiresAt \= NULL.

5\. If the order carries a voucher, Vouchers.UsedCount decreases by 1 (BR-44).

6\. Log the number of orders cancelled.

If the payment gateway reports success after this job cancelled the order: the transaction is recorded with Status \= Success and NeedsRefund \= 1, the order stays Cancelled, no subscription is created, and the transaction appears in the Manager's refund list (BR-47).

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | The job does not retry within the run; the next run (1 minute later) processes the same orders. Logs a critical error. Orders remain Pending in the meantime. |
| Error while processing one order (for example, the voucher return fails) | Rolls back that whole order, including the cancellation and slot release, because these steps must succeed or fail together. Logs a warning. Other orders are still processed; the failed order is processed again in the next run. |
| No overdue orders | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.6 Expire Timed-Out Payment Transactions (JOB-06)** {#13.6-expire-timed-out-payment-transactions-(job-06)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every minute, independently of JOB-05. If both jobs pick up the same transaction, the state re-check makes the second one skip it.

**Purpose:** Closes transactions whose payment link has expired, so the order returns to a state where the customer can press "Thanh toán lại" (Pay again). The transaction becomes Expired; the order stays Pending.

**Related:** UC-22, UC-37, UC-PAY · Rules CBR-69, CBR-40, DBR-41, DBR-42

**Parameters:** Online payment-link validity — 5 minutes from link creation, never beyond the order's payment deadline (deployment setting, no Manager screen — see System Parameters "Not configurable").

Processing steps:

1\. Find transactions with PaymentMethod \= OnlineGateway, Status \= Pending and ExpiresAt earlier than now. ExpiresAt is calculated when the link is created, as the earlier of link creation time \+ 5 minutes and Orders.PaymentDueAt; the job only reads it and never recalculates it.

2\. For each transaction, re-check that it is still Pending, then set Status \= Expired (CompletedAt stays NULL). The order stays Pending and any held slot stays Held (CBR-40).

3\. Log the number of transactions expired.

While the order is still valid, the customer presses "Thanh toán lại" to create a new link. The gateway's official result is still recorded through API-02 even if it arrives after the transaction expired; this job does not block it.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | The job does not retry within the run; the next run (1 minute later) processes the same transactions. Logs a critical error. Timed-out transactions remain Pending in the meantime, which only delays the "Pay again" button. |
| Error while processing one transaction | Rolls back that transaction only and logs a warning. Other transactions are still processed; the failed transaction is processed again in the next run. |
| No timed-out transactions | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

 

### **13.7 Remind and Auto-Reject Overdue Leave Requests (JOB-07)** {#13.7-remind-and-auto-reject-overdue-leave-requests-(job-07)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every minute

**Purpose:** Enforces the approval cut-off for leave requests: reminds the Managers as the cut-off approaches, then automatically rejects the request and notifies the staff member.

**Related:** UC-09, UC-14, UC-15 · Rules CBR-85, CBR-84, DBR-44

**Parameters:** Leave-approval cut-off — default 20:00 on the day before the leave date (P-20)

Processing steps:

1\. A request's cut-off \= the time in P-20 (default 20:00) on the day before LeaveDate. Example: leave on Thursday → cut-off is 20:00 Wednesday.

2\. Remind: from 2 hours before the cut-off (18:00 with default settings), the requests for the next day's leave that are still Pending and have ReminderSentAt \= NULL are listed in one system notification (SentByEmployeeId \= NULL, Audience \= Individual) with one NotificationRecipients row per active Manager account; ReminderSentAt is then set to now on each listed request, so each request is reminded once.

3\. Auto-reject: for each Pending request past its cut-off, re-check that it is still Pending, then set Status \= Rejected, RejectReason \= "Quá hạn duyệt" (display text of CBR-85 'Approval deadline passed'), ReviewedAt \= now, ReviewedByEmployeeId \= NULL (System).

4\. Send a system notification (Audience \= Individual) to the account of the employee who submitted the request.

5\. Log the number of requests reminded and auto-rejected.

Open issue: whether leave requests submitted by a Manager follow this job is pending the UC-15 decision.

Failure behavior:

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | The job does not retry within the run; the next run (1 minute later) processes the same requests. Logs a critical error. Reminders and auto-rejections are delayed; overdue requests remain Pending in the meantime. |
| Reminder notification cannot be sent | Logs a warning and skips that reminder (reminders are best-effort). The auto-reject step still runs normally. |
| Staff notification cannot be sent | Logs a warning. The request stays Rejected; the rejection is not rolled back. |
| Error while processing one request | Rolls back that request only and logs a warning. Other requests are still processed; the failed request is processed again in the next run. |
| No pending requests | Job completes immediately with no action — this is normal and expected. |

## **14\. External API Inventory** {#14.-external-api-inventory}

### **14.1 VNPay Payment Request (API-01)** {#14.1-vnpay-payment-request-(api-01)}

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| URL | GET redirect to the VNPay payment URL from deployment configuration (vnpay.pay-url; sandbox https\://sandbox.vnpayment.vn/paymentv2/vpcpay.html), API version 2.1.0. Parameters: vnp\_Version=2.1.0, vnp\_Command=pay, vnp\_TmnCode, vnp\_Amount \= Transactions.Amount × 100, vnp\_CurrCode=VND, vnp\_TxnRef, vnp\_OrderInfo (ASCII, Vietnamese marks removed), vnp\_OrderType=other, vnp\_Locale=vn, vnp\_ReturnUrl, vnp\_IpAddr, vnp\_CreateDate and vnp\_ExpireDate (yyyyMMddHHmmss, GMT+7), vnp\_SecureHash. |
| Purpose | Creates a signed payment request for a Pending online order and redirects the customer to the gateway (UC-22, UC-37, UC-PAY). vnp\_TxnRef \= order code without hyphens \+ "A" \+ attempt number (for example DH20260001A2); it is stored in Transactions.GatewayReference when the transaction is created and is how API-02 finds the transaction. vnp\_Amount is the amount stored on the transaction. vnp\_ExpireDate \= Transactions.ExpiresAt \= the earlier of creation time \+ 5 minutes and Orders.PaymentDueAt. Return URL: GET /payment/vnpay-return (vnpay.return-url, public). The page verifies the signature, then shows the transaction status read from the database; if the IPN has not arrived yet it shows "Đang xử lý thanh toán" and never changes any order, transaction or slot. |
| Caller | GMS (outbound) |
| Auth | Terminal code (vnp\_TmnCode) \+ vnp\_SecureHash \= HMAC-SHA512 (key \= vnpay.hash-secret, stored in deployment configuration) over the non-empty vnp\_\* parameters sorted by name, joined as key=URL-encoded value with "&", as lowercase hex. |

### **14.2 VNPay IPN Webhook (API-02)** {#14.2-vnpay-ipn-webhook-(api-02)}

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| URL | GET (POST also accepted): /api/v1/commerce/payment/webhook/vnpay — the URL is registered as the IPN URL on the VNPay merchant portal. It is excluded from the sign-in filter and needs no session. |
| Purpose | Receives the official payment result from VNPay and records it as a transaction (UC-PAY). This is the only place an order is marked as paid. Valid success (vnp\_ResponseCode and vnp\_TransactionStatus both "00", order still Pending, amount matches): Transactions.Status \= Success, GatewayReference kept, CompletedAt \= now; Orders.Status \= Paid, PaidAt \= now; the subscription is created (UC-PAY) and a held slot becomes Booked with its session Scheduled (CBR-53). All of this happens in one database transaction. Order already Cancelled or amount does not match: the transaction is set to Success with NeedsRefund \= 1; an order that is still Pending becomes Cancelled with CancelType \= InvalidPayment, its voucher use is returned (BR-44) and its held slot returns to Free (DBR-36); no subscription is created and the transaction appears in the Manager's refund list (BR-47). Payment failed (vnp\_ResponseCode or vnp\_TransactionStatus is not "00"): the transaction becomes Failed with FailureReason \= the VNPay code and CompletedAt \= now; the order stays Pending and its slot stays Held, so the customer can pay again before the deadline (CBR-69). Response to VNPay — JSON {"RspCode","Message"}: 00 Confirm Success (processed, including success-with-refund); 01 Order not found (no transaction with this vnp\_TxnRef); 02 Order already confirmed (repeated callback, nothing changes); 04 Invalid amount (recorded per CBR-72); 97 Invalid signature (nothing recorded); 99 Unknown error. |
| Caller | VNPay payment gateway (server-to-server) |
| Auth | HMAC-SHA512 signature validation (vnp\_SecureHash, key \= vnpay.hash-secret); the endpoint is public but every request must carry a valid signature, otherwise it is rejected with RspCode 97\. |

### **14.3 Email Delivery (API-03)** {#14.3-email-delivery-(api-03)}

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| URL | SMTP smtp.gmail.com:587 with STARTTLS required (TLS 1.2 or 1.3), host and port from deployment configuration (mail.smtp.host, mail.smtp.port); client library Jakarta Mail (Eclipse Angus Mail). |
| Purpose | Sends 6-digit verification codes for sign-up (SignUp, UC-05), profile claim (Claim, UC-Claim), password recovery (Recovery, UC-03), email change (EmailChange — code to the new email) and phone change (PhoneChange — code to the current email) in Account Settings (UC-04, CBR-110), and a notice to the old email when the login email changes (CBR-29). Codes expire after P-15 (default 15 minutes) and can be used once. An account created at the counter receives no email; the customer sets a password through Forgot Password (CBR-31). Sender display name "Super Gym", subject prefix "\[Super Gym\]", body sent as plain text plus HTML. Connection, read and write timeouts are 10 seconds each; a timeout counts as a failed send. If sending fails, nothing is saved (no account, no code, no change) and the user sees MSG04 "Hệ thống đang bận. Vui lòng thử lại sau ít phút."; if the old-email notice of CBR-29 fails, the email change is still kept and a warning is logged. When no app password is configured (development), the email is printed to the server console instead of sent. The system never sends SMS. |
| Caller | GMS (outbound) |
| Auth | SMTP account (mail.username) \+ app password (mail.app-password), stored in deployment configuration |

### **14.4 Weather Forecast (API-04)** {#14.4-weather-forecast-(api-04)}

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| URL | GET https\://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=…\&longitude=…\&current=temperature\_2m,apparent\_temperature,relative\_humidity\_2m,weather\_code,is\_day\&daily=weather\_code,temperature\_2m\_max,temperature\_2m\_min,precipitation\_probability\_max\&timezone=Asia/Ho\_Chi\_Minh\&forecast\_days=1 |
| Purpose | Shows today's weather at the gym on the PT Dashboard (9.1.2). Location from deployment configuration (weather.latitude, weather.longitude; default Hà Nội 21.0285, 105.8542). Results are cached in memory for 30 minutes and shared by all users. If the call fails, returns a non-200 status or takes more than 3 seconds (connect and response timeout), the weather card is hidden and the rest of the page loads normally; the failure is remembered for 5 minutes before the next attempt. |
| Caller | GMS (outbound) |
| Auth | None (public API, no key) |

# **III. Requirement Appendix** {#iii.-requirement-appendix}

\[Provide business rules, common requirements, or other extra requirements information here\]

## **1\. General Business Rules** {#1.-general-business-rules}

\[Provide common business rules that you must follow. The information can be provided in the table format as the sample below\] 

| GBR-ID | Rule Statement | Applies To | Rationale | Enforced By |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GBR-01 | The interface is Vietnamese. Dates are dd/mm/yyyy, times are 24-hour HH:mm, and all times use the gym’s time zone (UTC+7). Enumerated values are stored in English and displayed in Vietnamese. | All screens | Staff and members are Vietnamese; one time zone avoids off-by-one-day errors in expiry and attendance. | The system automatically on every screen and stored time |
| GBR-02 | All amounts are whole Vietnamese dong. Catalogue prices already include VAT — exactly what the customer sees and pays; the VAT rate is configured by the Manager and copied into each order. Screens show VAT as a breakdown, never as an extra charge. | All sales, payment and report screens | Customers pay exactly the listed price; VAT is shown for tax reporting without changing the price. | The system automatically on every price, order and report |
| GBR-03 | The end date of every package, freeze, voucher and report period is the last valid day. A one-month package starting 05/09 ends on 05/10 and can be used for the whole of 05/10; the next package starts 06/10. If the target day does not exist in the target month (start 30/01 or 31/01), the last day of that month is used. | All dated records | Customers get the full last day they paid for; all modules count dates the same way. | The system automatically when computing end dates |
| GBR-04 | Business limits are parameters P-01…P-21 with agreed defaults (freeze count and length, minimum staffing, VAT, default commission, payment deadline, leave cut-offs, attendance window, swap limit, lock policy…). A change applies only to records created afterwards; each order keeps the payment deadline it was created with. | All modules | The Manager can adjust business limits without a code change; existing orders stay as sold. | The system automatically, reading SystemConfigs at the time a record is created |
| GBR-05 | No business record is ever physically deleted; “delete” always switches it to Inactive, so history (sessions taught, transactions handled) stays intact. | All entities | History, revenue and tax records must stay complete and traceable. | The system automatically on every delete action |
| GBR-06 | A record cannot be deactivated while another active record still refers to it. | All entities | Prevents orphan or broken references (e.g. a PT with future sessions). | The system automatically before every deactivation |
| GBR-07 | Every sensitive action — price change, account action, deletion, approval or rejection — is written to the audit log. | All modules | Lets the Admin trace who changed money, accounts and decisions. | The system automatically on every sensitive action |
| GBR-08 | Each audit line reads as a plain sentence: who – did what – to what – from which value to which value – when – why. Only the Admin can read the log. | Audit log | The Admin can read the log without technical knowledge. | The system automatically when writing the audit log |
| GBR-09 | Every rejection of a pending request, and every cancellation, deletion, void or cash variance, requires a written reason (at least 5 characters) that is stored with the record and in the audit log. | All approval and cancellation actions | Negative decisions must be explainable to customers and staff. | The system on submit (reason required, 5–500 characters) |
| GBR-10 | Each action can be performed only by the roles allowed in the role & permission matrix (Guest, Customer, PT, Receptionist, Manager, Admin); users see and change only the data their role allows. | All screens | Each role sees and does only what its job requires. | The system on every page and request (role filter) |
| GBR-11 | Bookings, PT availability, PT package sessions and check-ins must all fall within the configured opening hours. | Scheduling, booking, check-in | Nothing can be booked or used while the gym is closed. | The system automatically on every time-based action |
| GBR-12 | Everyone who uses a service — members, dependants and walk-ins — has exactly one active customer profile. | All customer-facing features | Avoids duplicate members and split purchase history. | The system on profile creation (phone/email duplicate check) |
| GBR-13 | Every rule checked on a screen is checked again on the server; the server never trusts values sent by the interface. Competing actions on the same record are resolved by database constraints — the later request is refused. | All modules | Values sent from the browser can be altered. | The system on the server for every request |
| GBR-14 | Time-based rules run without user action: package expiry, freeze resume, attendance auto-close, PT package expiry, payment deadline and slot release, leave auto-rejection. | All time-based states | Statuses stay correct even when nobody is at the counter. | Background jobs running daily (00:05, UTC+7) or every few minutes |
| GBR-15 | Verification codes are sent by email only; there is no SMS. In-app notifications reach users who have an account; dependants are informed outside the system. | Notifications, sign-up, recovery | Email is free and reliable; SMS is out of scope. | The system when sending codes and notifications |
| GBR-16 | Refunds, invoices / e-invoices and cost of goods are handled outside the system; the system only records what is needed to trigger or reconcile them. | Sales, payment, reports | Keeps the project scope; accounting is done in the gym's existing tools. | Business process (outside the system) |
| GBR-17 | Required fields are marked \*. Validation runs when leaving a field and again on submit; each error appears in red under its field. | All forms | Users fix errors before submitting, without losing input. | The system on blur and on submit |
| GBR-18 | Lists show 10 rows by default (10 / 20 / 50 selectable); paging applies after search and filters, and changing a filter returns to page 1\. Default order is newest first. | All lists | Long lists stay fast and readable. | The system on every list |
| GBR-19 | Keywords are trimmed, case-insensitive and diacritic-insensitive (“nguyen” matches “Nguyễn”). | All lists | Vietnamese names are found whether typed with or without diacritics. | The system on every search box |
| GBR-20 | Filters combine with AND; “Clear filters” restores the defaults. | All lists | Predictable, narrowing filters. | The system on every filtered list |
| GBR-21 | An empty list shows a short message: nothing yet, no result for the search, or no data in the chosen period. | All lists and reports | The user knows the list is empty rather than broken. | The system on every list and report |
| GBR-22 | The submit button is disabled while a request is processed; success shows a toast; on error the form keeps the user’s input. | All forms | Prevents double submission and lost input. | The system on every form |
| GBR-23 | Irreversible or destructive actions (delete, cancel, void, reject, deactivate, publish) ask for confirmation first. | All destructive actions | Prevents irreversible mistakes. | The system before every destructive action |
| GBR-24 | Leaving a form with unsaved changes asks the user to confirm. | All forms | Prevents losing typed data. | The system when leaving a form |
| GBR-25 | Fields the current user may not edit are greyed out with a hint saying who can change them. | All forms | The user knows why a field is locked and whom to ask. | The system on every form |
| GBR-26 | Dates or slots that break a rule are shown but disabled, with the reason on hover. | All date and slot pickers | The user sees why an option is unavailable. | The system on every date or slot picker |
| GBR-27 | Time-limited states (payment deadline, slot hold, verification code, temporary lock) show an mm:ss countdown and refresh when it reaches zero. | Payment, booking, sign-in | The user knows how long a hold or code is still valid. | The system on every time-limited state |
| GBR-28 | Green \= active / successful, amber \= pending / held, red \= rejected / cancelled / failed, grey \= inactive / expired — the same on every screen. | All status badges | Statuses are recognised at a glance. | The system on every status badge |
| GBR-29 | Amounts are right-aligned with a thousand separator and “đ”; totals show “incl. VAT x%”. | All amounts | Amounts are easy to read and compare. | The system on every money field |
| GBR-30 | Password fields are masked with a show/hide toggle. | Sign-in, sign-up, account | Prevents shoulder surfing while allowing a check of what was typed. | The system on every password field |
| GBR-31 | When the sign-in session expires, the user signs in again and returns to the same screen. | All signed-in screens | Users do not lose their place after a time-out. | The system on every authenticated page (session time-out 2 hours) |
| GBR-32 | If a record changed since it was opened, saving is refused and the user is asked to reload. | All edit forms | Prevents one user silently overwriting another. | The system on save (row version check) |
| GBR-33 | Exports contain exactly the rows matching the current search and filters. | Lists and reports with export | The export matches what the user sees. | The system on every export |
| GBR-34 | Toasts disappear after 3–5 seconds, error toasts stay until closed; user notifications keep a read / unread state. | All screens | Feedback is visible but not intrusive. | The system on every toast and notification |
| GBR-35 | Screens used on the gym floor (PT dashboard, session attendance) work on a phone-sized screen. | PT screens | PTs work on the gym floor with a phone. | The system (responsive layout) on those screens |

## **2\. Common Business Rules** {#2.-common-business-rules}

| CBR-ID | Rule Statement | Use Case Relevant |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| CBR-01 | A New customer becomes Active as soon as their first membership package or day pass is paid. Paying for a PT package does not change the member state. | UC-20, UC-22, UC-PAY |
| CBR-02 | An Expired member becomes Active again as soon as a new membership package or day pass is paid. Paying for a PT package does not change the member state. | UC-20, UC-22, UC-PAY |
| CBR-03 | When the membership package reaches its end date, an Active member becomes Expired. | UC-19, UC-41 |
| CBR-04 | Nobody may edit an Inactive profile. The Receptionist cannot see it, the Manager sees it read-only, and the Admin traces its history through the audit log. | UC-08, UC-16, UC-17 |
| CBR-05 | A New customer may buy a first membership package or day pass, but not a PT package (CBR-59). | UC-20, UC-22 |
| CBR-06 | An Expired member may buy a new membership package or day pass to continue; buying a PT package requires a valid membership package first (CBR-59). | UC-20, UC-22 |
| CBR-07 | The maximum number of freezes per package is configured by the Manager (default: 1). | UC-09, UC-18 |
| CBR-08 | The maximum freeze duration is configured by the Manager (default: 1 month). | UC-09, UC-18 |
| CBR-09 | Changing a package price or description in the catalogue never applies retroactively to existing orders. | UC-09, UC-20, UC-21, UC-22 |
| CBR-10 | The price of an existing order cannot be edited. A wrong order is cancelled and a new one is created. | UC-20, UC-21 |
| CBR-11 | The Receptionist may cancel a Paid counter order only within the shift that created it and before the shift is closed; the money is returned to the customer at the counter. | UC-20, UC-25 |
| CBR-12 | Every price belongs to a specific package in the catalogue; there are no free-standing prices. | UC-09, UC-10 |
| CBR-13 | Customers under 10 years old cannot buy a single PT package. | UC-16, UC-21 |
| CBR-14 | Customers under 10 years old cannot buy a couple PT package. | UC-16, UC-21 |
| CBR-15 | Customers under 10 years old cannot book a single PT session. | UC-21, UC-37 |
| CBR-16 | A member who still has a running package or unused PT sessions goes to Pending deletion and waits for Manager approval. | UC-16, UC-17 |
| CBR-17 | A customer profile and a login account are separate things: a profile may exist without an account. | UC-04, UC-05, UC-16 |
| CBR-18 | A login account is optional. Dependent profiles and profiles that only buy day passes have no account. | UC-05, UC-16, UC-Claim |
| CBR-19 | If the Receptionist enters a phone number that matches an active Person, the system opens that Person's customer profile. If the Person has no customer profile that is not Inactive (for example an employee), the Receptionist checks an identity document and creates the customer profile on the same Person instead of a new Person (CBR-114).  | UC-16, UC-IDENT |
| CBR-20 | If a guest signs up with the phone number of an active self-owned profile that has no account and enters the same email as the profile, the system sends a verification code to that email instead of creating a new profile; after the correct code and a password, the account is attached to the existing profile. | UC-05, UC-Claim |
| CBR-21 | A Dependent profile has no login account. | UC-04, UC-05 |
| CBR-22 | The guardian only needs to be present at registration, not at every session. | UC-16, UC-19 |
| CBR-23 | If a phone number matches no active Person (only Inactive ones), a new Person and profile are created normally.  | UC-16, UC-IDENT |
| CBR-24 | When the Receptionist creates a profile for a customer buying a package of one month or longer, the Receptionist also creates the login account with the Person's email (CBR-31). If the Person already has an account (for example an employee), no second account is created: the existing account now also serves the customer role (DBR-65).  | UC-16, UC-20 |
| CBR-25 | A guest signing up with the phone number of a self-owned profile that has no account, but with a different email from the one on the profile, cannot activate it. The system says the phone number is registered with another email (masked); the guest uses that email or asks the Receptionist to verify and update it. | UC-05, UC-Claim |
| CBR-26 | If a guest signs up with the phone number of an active Person that already has a login account, no account or profile is created; the system says the number already has an account and points to Sign In / Forgot Password, without saying whose number it is. An employee who also wants to train as a customer gets the customer profile at the counter (CBR-19), never through online sign-up.  | UC-03, UC-05 |
| CBR-27 | A self-owned profile without an email cannot be activated online; the customer goes to the counter so the Receptionist can add the email and create the account (CBR-24). | UC-05, UC-16, UC-Claim |
| CBR-28 | Duplicate checks during self sign-up only compare against the phone number on Person; guardian numbers recorded on Dependent profiles neither block nor activate anything — the guardian registers as a new customer.  | UC-05, UC-IDENT |
| CBR-29 | When the email of an account changes, by the account holder (UC-04) or by the Receptionist (UC-16), the system notifies the old email and signs out every session of that account except the one that made the change. The email is stored on Person, so the change applies to every role of that Person.  | UC-04, UC-16 |
| CBR-30 | In their own account a customer can change only the avatar, email, phone number and password. Full name, date of birth, check-in photo and guardian details are changed by the Receptionist (UC-16), because they are used for check-in verification and the PT age rule. Email and phone number changes follow CBR-110. | UC-04, UC-16 |
| CBR-31 | An account created by the Receptionist (CBR-24) has no password and no email is sent. It cannot sign in until the customer sets a password through Forgot Password (UC-03); until then every sign-in attempt says the account has no password yet and points to Forgot Password.  | UC-01, UC-03, UC-16 |
| CBR-32 | A Dependent profile has no self-service channel: it cannot view schedules, book single sessions, reschedule or cancel PT sessions itself. Packages and single sessions are bought at the counter (UC-21, CBR-54); PT sessions are rescheduled by the PT at the guardian's request (BR-62); schedules are checked with the Receptionist or the PT. Cancellation is not supported — an absent customer's session becomes Missed, the same result as cancelling (BR-78). | UC-16, UC-21, UC-35 |
| CBR-33 | Before acting on behalf of a Dependent profile, the PT or Receptionist verifies the requester with one of the guardian phone numbers recorded on the profile (DBR-25) or the customer code.  | UC-16, UC-21, UC-35 |
| CBR-34 | A paid day pass is valid immediately. | UC-20, UC-PAY |
| CBR-35 | A check-in photo is mandatory for every package except the day pass; the Receptionist takes it at the counter when the customer first buys a package. | UC-16, UC-20 |
| CBR-36 | A day pass gives exactly one entry to the gym. | UC-19, UC-20 |
| CBR-37 | The avatar uploaded by the customer is for display only and is never used for check-in verification. | UC-04, UC-16, UC-19 |
| CBR-38 | The check-in photo belongs to the customer profile, not to the account. Only the Receptionist can take or retake it; the customer cannot change or delete it, even with an account. | UC-04, UC-16, UC-19 |
| CBR-39 | When booking a single session or swapping by themselves, customers can only choose slots in the current week (today to Sunday). From Saturday, slots of the following week also become available. The Receptionist scheduling a PT package and a PT rescheduling or transferring a session are not bound by this limit. | UC-37, UC-38 |
| CBR-40 | The hold lasts exactly as long as the order's payment deadline (P-09, copied into the order at creation — GBR-04); there is no separate slot timer. A Failed or Expired transaction does not release the slot: the order is still Pending, so the slot stays Held and the customer can pay again within the deadline (CBR-69). | UC-37, UC-PAY |
| CBR-41 | A customer can hold slots for only one Pending single-session order at a time. Creating a new single-session order while an older one is Pending cancels the older order (type: replaced by a new order — CBR-71) and returns its slot to Free. | UC-37, UC-PAY |
| CBR-42 | When the attendance window (BR-54) ends and the session is still Scheduled: if the customer (couple: at least one of them) checked in that day, the session becomes Completed; otherwise it becomes Missed (reason: no check-in). CBR-64 takes precedence (reason: no membership package). | UC-31, UC-32 |
| CBR-43 | Each PT package has exactly one fixed time slot, applied to every Monday-to-Friday within the package term. The slot differs only on days where the Receptionist had to pick another time because the fixed slot was taken (BR-41), on swapped sessions (the swap rules) and on sessions rescheduled or transferred by the PT (the PT session-handling rules). | UC-21, UC-38 |
| CBR-44 | A session can only be swapped into a slot the PT has published as available. | UC-30, UC-38 |
| CBR-45 | For customers, a swap is the only way to move a session to Saturday or Sunday themselves. A PT rescheduling or transferring a session (BR-64, BR-65) is not restricted to weekdays. | UC-21, UC-38 |
| CBR-46 | After a reschedule, transfer or cancellation, the system notifies the customer immediately (couple: both members), and on a transfer also the new PT. | UC-32, UC-35, UC-36 |
| CBR-47 | The system does not handle the case where one member of a couple package drops out. | UC-21, UC-31 |
| CBR-48 | PT packages (single and couple) are not sold online; they are sold at the counter only. | UC-21, UC-22 |
| CBR-49 | Single and couple PT packages are paid at the counter in cash or by bank transfer only. A single session booked online is paid through the online gateway (CBR-53); a single session bought at the counter is paid in cash or by transfer (CBR-54). | UC-21, UC-37, UC-PAY |
| CBR-50 | When a PT package order is Paid, the system creates all of its sessions in state Scheduled. | UC-21, UC-32 |
| CBR-51 | The customer cannot change PT midway when the PT is not at fault. | UC-21, UC-38 |
| CBR-52 | The fixed time slot of a PT package is agreed directly between the customer and the PT before the order is created, and must be one of the PT's published available slots. | UC-21, UC-30 |
| CBR-53 | Booking a single session: choose a PT → choose a time from the PT's published schedule → the system creates a Pending order and holds the slot immediately (Held — DBR-36) → the customer pays within the order deadline → when the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked and the session is created. If the deadline passes unpaid, the slot returns to Free. | UC-37, UC-PAY |
| CBR-54 | When the customer confirms, the system creates a Pending order and the slot becomes Held immediately for the order's payment deadline (P-09, default 20 minutes, shown as an mm:ss countdown — GBR-27). When the order is Paid the slot becomes Booked and the session is created; if the deadline passes unpaid, the order is Cancelled and the slot returns to Free. A Failed or Expired transaction keeps the slot Held while the order is still within its deadline (CBR-40, CBR-69).  | UC-21, UC-PAY |
| CBR-55 | When a PT package passes its end date, the subscription becomes Expired automatically. Any Scheduled session left in the package (after reschedules or transfers) becomes Cancelled at the same time, with no refund and no term extension. | UC-21, UC-32, UC-36 |
| CBR-56 | Sessions are still generated on a date declared closed. Before that date the PT must reschedule them (PtReschedule, no swap quota used). | CBR-57 | If a closed day is declared after the order is Paid, the session on that day becomes Cancelled with reason 'gym closed', is not deducted and is not refunded; the customer and PT are notified and the term is unchanged. | CBR-58 | A PT package or a single session only pays for the trainer; it does not include gym access. Gym access comes only from a membership package or a day pass. | UC-19, UC-21, UC-37, UC-41 |
| CBR-59 | A PT package order (single or couple) can be created only for a customer who holds a valid membership package at that moment — a day pass or a frozen membership does not count. An employee who also trains as a customer must choose a different PT (CBR-115).  | UC-20, UC-21 |
| CBR-60 | A single session can be booked only on a date covered by a valid membership package, or for today if the customer holds a valid day pass (CBR-34, BR-32). | CBR-61 | A swap (UC-38) or a PT reschedule/transfer (UC-35) may only target a date on which the customer still holds a valid membership package; for a couple package, at least one member must hold one on that date. | UC-35, UC-38 |
| CBR-62 | A freeze is never blocked by PT sessions. The PT package and the membership are two separate packages: a freeze applies only to the membership (BR-21), so the PT package term does not move. Before saving, the system lists every session that will become Missed so the Receptionist can inform the customer. | UC-18, UC-31, UC-36 |

| CBR-67 | A couple-package session inside one member's freeze period becomes Missed only if the other member also holds no valid membership on that day; otherwise it stays Scheduled so the other member can still train (BR-56). | UC-18, UC-31 |

| CBR-69 | When a transaction becomes Failed or Expired the order stays Pending; the customer can pay again for the same order while it is within its deadline. | UC-22, UC-37, UC-PAY |

| CBR-71 | When a customer creates a new online order for the same package while an older online order for it is Pending, the older order becomes Cancelled (type: replaced by a new order). | UC-22, UC-37 |
| CBR-72 | If the gateway reports success but the order is already Cancelled or the amount does not match, the transaction is still recorded as Success, the order is not Paid (if not yet cancelled it becomes Cancelled, type: invalid payment), no entitlement is created, and the transaction goes to the Manager's refund list. | UC-26, UC-37, UC-PAY |

| CBR-74 | Each customer may use a voucher at most the number of times configured on it (default 1; empty \= unlimited). Uses are counted on orders held by the customer that are not Cancelled, including Pending ones; for a couple package only the holder is counted. | UC-12, UC-23 |
| CBR-75 | A voucher cannot be added, removed or changed while the order has a Pending transaction. | UC-23, UC-PAY |
| CBR-76 | Each voucher has a scope chosen by the Manager: membership packages & day passes (default) or membership packages only. PT packages and single sessions never accept a voucher; the PT sale screen has no voucher field. | UC-12, UC-23 |
| CBR-77 | The Receptionist confirms a bank transfer at the counter only after checking that the money has arrived in the gym's account. | UC-20, UC-21, UC-PAY |
| CBR-78 | The Receptionist can close a shift only when no counter order created in that shift is still Pending: each must be paid or cancelled (type: cancelled by the Receptionist) first. | UC-20, UC-21, UC-25 |
| CBR-79 | The cost of goods is outside the system's scope. | UC-09, UC-46 |
| CBR-80 | A Missed session earns the PT commission like a Completed one, because the customer's absence is not the PT's fault. | UC-31, UC-46 |
| CBR-81 | A session cancelled by the PT under BR-66 earns commission like a Completed one, because the PT has repaid the customer in cash. | UC-35, UC-46 |
| CBR-82 | A session cancelled by the customer (BR-78) earns commission like a Completed one. | UC-39, UC-46 |
| CBR-83 | A PT cannot request leave for a time when they still have a Scheduled session. Since a PT teaching a term-based package is booked every Monday to Friday (BR-40), the PT must first handle every session on that day under the PT session-handling rules — reschedule, transfer or cancel — before the request can be submitted. The request form lists the blocking sessions with a link to the session-handling screen (9.4.1). | UC-14, UC-35 |
| CBR-84 | A leave request must be submitted before the submission cut-off on the day before the leave (P-12, default 15:00). After the cut-off the system shows 'Submission deadline passed' and blocks submission. Example: leave on Thursday → deadline 15:00 Wednesday. Unplanned absences are reported to the Manager directly, outside the system. | UC-09, UC-14 |
| CBR-85 | The Manager must decide a leave request before the approval cut-off on the day before the leave (P-20, default 20:00). Close to the cut-off the system reminds the Manager; after it, a Pending request becomes Rejected with reason 'Approval deadline passed' and the employee is notified. | UC-09, UC-14, UC-15 |
| CBR-86 | When a role of a Person becomes Inactive — the employee resigns (UC-13) or the customer profile is deleted (UC-16, UC-17) — every session of that Person's account is signed out immediately. If the Person still has another role that is not Inactive, the account stays Active and from then on serves only that role; otherwise the account becomes Inactive, which is final (DBR-28).  | UC-07, UC-13, UC-16, UC-17  |
| CBR-87 | An employee's position can change only when no unfinished work remains in the old position: a PT has no Scheduled session, no future slot and no running PT package; a Receptionist has no open shift. Changes to or from Admin follow BR-08. | UC-07, UC-13 |
| CBR-88 | Each shift must keep at least 2 PTs on duty. | UC-09, UC-14, UC-15 |
| CBR-89 | The Receptionist also looks after the gym facilities. | UC-28, UC-29 |
| CBR-90 | Each shift must keep at least 1 Receptionist on duty. | UC-09, UC-14, UC-15 |
| CBR-91 | A PT can edit only the private notes and workout/meal plans they created; everyone can edit only their own account profile. | UC-04, UC-24, UC-32, UC-33, UC-34, UC-40 |
| CBR-92 | A private note about a customer is visible only to the PT who wrote it — even after the customer moves to another PT, the new PT cannot see it. | UC-32, UC-33 |
| CBR-93 | After a successful password change in Account Settings (UC-04), every other session of that account is signed out; after a password reset through Forgot Password (UC-03), every session is signed out.  | UC-03, UC-04 |
| CBR-94 | A verification or recovery code allows 5 wrong entries (P-17). On the 5th wrong entry the code is cancelled and verification for that email is locked for 5 minutes (P-18) — no entry and no new code during the lock. Requesting a new code is allowed 60 seconds after the previous one; the 5th request within an hour triggers the same 5-minute lock. A new code always cancels the previous one.  | UC-03, UC-04, UC-05, UC-Claim |
| CBR-95 | Staff accounts (Admin, Manager, PT, Receptionist) are created only by the Admin. If the phone number matches an active Person (for example a customer), the staff role is attached to that Person instead of a new Person (CBR-114); if that Person already has an account, no second account is created — the existing account, with its email and password, now also serves the staff role (DBR-65). Customer accounts come from exactly two sources: online self sign-up (UC-05) or creation by the Receptionist at the counter (UC-16). The Admin never creates customer accounts. | UC-05, UC-07, UC-16  |
| CBR-96 | An account is blocked from signing in only in three cases: it is Inactive because every role of its Person is Inactive (CBR-86), the Admin has locked it, or it is temporarily locked under BR-01. | UC-01, UC-07 |
| CBR-97 | An Inactive package is no longer sold; running orders of that package are unaffected. | UC-10, UC-20, UC-22 |
| CBR-98 | A voucher used at least once can only be deactivated, never deleted. | UC-12, UC-23 |
| CBR-99 | A facility item cannot be deleted while it has a maintenance request that is not Closed. | UC-27, UC-29 |
| CBR-100 | A blog post switched to Inactive disappears from the public site immediately. | UC-06, UC-45 |
| CBR-101 | When the Manager approves a maintenance request, the facility item's condition switches to Under maintenance automatically, unless the Manager unticks 'Set item to Under maintenance' because the item can still be used while waiting for the repair.  | UC-27, UC-29 |
| CBR-102 | When the Receptionist closes a maintenance request, the facility item returns to Available automatically if it has no other request still In Progress.  | UC-27, UC-28 |
| CBR-103 | The audit log and audit-related metrics are visible to the Admin only; the Manager's report does not include them. | UC-46, UC-47 |
| CBR-104 | Each open day has exactly two duty shifts — morning and afternoon — generated automatically from the opening hours; there is no manual rostering. | UC-11, UC-25 |
| CBR-105 | The Receptionist on duty opens the shift at its start and closes it at its end; every payment taken while the shift is open is recorded in that shift. | UC-20, UC-25, UC-PAY |
| CBR-106 | Only the Manager can read customer feedback; PTs and Receptionists cannot. | UC-42, UC-43 |
| CBR-107 | Each piece of feedback has a submission time and a read/unread state. There is no reply or resolution workflow — the Manager only reads it. | UC-42, UC-43 |
| CBR-108 | In their own account a staff member can change only the avatar, email, phone number and password. Personnel details (full name, date of birth, specialty, years of experience, hire date, commission rate, employment status) are view-only for the staff member and changed by the Manager (CBR-108). Position is changed only by the Admin (CBR-109); the employee code never changes (DBR-09). Position and account status are view only and are changed only by the Admin (CBR-109). The employee code is system-generated and never changes (DBR-09). Full name and date of birth are stored once on Person: whether changed by the Manager (UC-13) or the Receptionist (UC-16), the change applies to every role of that Person and is logged (CBR-112). Email and phone number changes follow CBR-110.  | UC-04, UC-13 |
| CBR-109 | Role, position and account status (active / locked) are never editable in Account Settings. Only the Admin changes an employee's position (UC-07, CBR-87, BR-08) and locks or unlocks an account. A role is added by creating a customer profile (CBR-19) or a staff role (CBR-95) on the Person, never by editing the account. The only automatic changes are CBR-86 and the temporary lock of BR-01.  | UC-04, UC-07, UC-13  |
| CBR-110 | Changing the email or phone number in Account Settings (UC-04), customer or staff, requires a verification code: for a new email the code is sent to the new email; for a new phone number it is sent to the account's current email. The new value is checked for duplicates (DBR-22, DBR-23) before the code is sent and again when it is saved, and the value saved is exactly the one the code was issued for (GBR-13). Email and phone number are stored on Person, so the change applies to every role. Changes made at the counter by the Receptionist (BR-19) need no code.  | UC-04, UC-16  |
| CBR-111 | The Dependent profiles tab of Account Settings is shown only when the user is working in the Customer role (CBR-113); a staff role never sees it.  | UC-04, UC-16  |
| CBR-112 | Changes of email, phone number and password in Account Settings, and changes of the personal data stored on Person by the Manager or the Receptionist, are written to the audit log as readable sentences (GBR-08) that state the role the user was working in. Passwords and verification codes are never written to the log (DBR-02).  | UC-04, UC-08, UC-13, UC-16  |
| CBR-113 | A user signs in with email or phone number and password; either one identifies exactly one account (DBR-22, DBR-23, DBR-65). If the account serves more than one role that is not Inactive, the system asks which role to work in — the staff position or Customer — before opening any home screen. The session holds exactly one role, and every screen and permission follows that role (GBR-10). The user can switch role at any time from the account menu without signing in again; an account with a single role goes straight to that role's home screen. | UC-01, UC-02, UC-04  |
| CBR-114 | The phone number identifies the Person. When a customer profile or a staff role is created for a phone number that matches an active Person who does not hold that kind of role (DBR-65), the Receptionist or the Admin checks an identity document and attaches the new role to that Person: no second Person is created, and full name and date of birth are taken from the Person, not entered again. This happens only at the counter (CBR-19) and in staff account creation (CBR-95); online sign-up never attaches a role to an existing Person (CBR-26). | UC-05, UC-07, UC-16  |
| CBR-115 | A Person must not act in a staff role on their own customer profile: when the signed-in staff role and the customer profile belong to the same Person, the system blocks selling or changing a package, applying a voucher, freezing, editing or deleting the profile, approving its deletion, refunding, and any PT booking, cancellation, attendance, note or plan in which the same Person is both trainee and PT. Another employee with the required permission performs the action instead.  | UC-16, UC-17, UC-18, UC-19, UC-20, UC-21, UC-23, UC-31, UC-33, UC-34, UC-35, UC-37  |

## **3\. Business Rules** {#3.-business-rules}

| BR-ID | Rule Statement | Use Case Relevant |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-01 | An account that serves only the Customer role and enters a wrong password 5 times in a row is locked for 5 minutes (P-17, P-18). An account that serves any staff role, including one that also serves the Customer role, is never locked automatically — counter machines are shared, and a wrong lock would stop a whole shift from taking payments or checking customers in. | UC-01 |
| BR-02 | When the temporary lock (BR-01) ends, the customer account unlocks and the failure counter resets to 0\. A successful sign-in also resets the counter. | UC-01 |
| BR-03 | Password recovery verifies only through the registered email of the account: the user starts recovery by entering the email, and the code is sent only to that email (GBR-15). | UC-03 |
| BR-04 | A password recovery code expires after 15 minutes (P-15). | UC-03 |
| BR-05 | Withdrawn in v25 — replaced by CBR-110. | UC-04 |
| BR-06 | The system must always have at least one active Admin account. | UC-07 |
| BR-07 | The last active Admin account cannot be deleted, locked or demoted, and its employee record cannot be set to Resigned. | UC-07 |
| BR-08 | Only an Admin can create an Admin account or promote someone to Admin. | UC-07 |
| BR-09 | The Admin can unlock a temporarily locked customer account early. | UC-07 |
| BR-10 | When the Admin unlocks an account — locked manually or temporarily after failed sign-ins — a reason of 5–500 characters is required. The unlock resets the failed-attempt counter to 0 and is written to the audit log together with the reason. | UC-07 |
| BR-11 | The gym's financial parameters are: package prices, VAT, PT commission rate and fees. | UC-09 |
| BR-12 | The gym has one default opening and closing time for every day; the Manager declares only the days that differ (e.g. Sunday, public holidays). | UC-11 |
| BR-13 | An Inactive employee no longer appears in the list of working staff. | UC-13 |
| BR-14 | The Manager cannot approve a leave request if, after approval, the remaining staff of that shift (DBR-60) would fall below CBR-88 or CBR-90. Example: with exactly 2 PTs left, no PT may take leave; with exactly 1 Receptionist left, that Receptionist may not take leave. | UC-15 |
| BR-15 | A member with no running package and no unused PT session is deleted immediately. | UC-16 |
| BR-16 | The Receptionist cannot delete on their own a profile that still has a running package or unused PT sessions. | UC-16 |
| BR-17 | Every deletion of a customer profile requires a reason. | UC-16 |
| BR-18 | A profile cannot change between Dependent and self-owned. When a child gets their own phone number, the current package runs out, the old profile is deleted and a new self-owned profile is created. | UC-16 |
| BR-19 | The Receptionist changes the phone number or email of a customer profile that has an account only when the customer is at the counter and has been checked against the check-in photo; if the profile has no check-in photo yet, the Receptionist checks an identity document and takes the check-in photo on the spot. The change applies to every role of that Person (CBR-110). | UC-16 |
| BR-20 | When the Receptionist freezes the package of an Active member, the member becomes Frozen. | UC-18 |
| BR-21 | Only a membership package can be frozen; PT packages (single and couple) cannot. | UC-18 |
| BR-22 | Freezing a membership package is free of charge. | UC-18 |
| BR-23 | An expired package cannot be frozen. | UC-18 |
| BR-24 | A package that has used up its freeze allowance cannot be frozen again. | UC-18 |
| BR-25 | When the freeze period ends, the package reopens automatically and the member returns to Active; the Receptionist does nothing. | UC-18 |
| BR-26 | The Receptionist may cancel a freeze early: the package reopens immediately, the member returns to Active and the end date is extended only by the days actually frozen (DBR-51). The freeze allowance stays used (BR-24, P-01), and PT sessions already switched to Missed by the freeze are not restored (CBR-68). | UC-18 |
| BR-27 | A member with canUseService \= FALSE cannot check in. | UC-19 |
| BR-28 | Check-in only needs the customer code or phone number; no card and no login account are required. | UC-19 |
| BR-29 | A day pass stops being valid as soon as the customer checks in with it. | UC-19 |
| BR-30 | A day pass needs no check-in photo and no face comparison. | UC-19 |
| BR-31 | When checking in a customer holding a package of one month or longer, the Receptionist compares the customer's face with the check-in photo shown on screen. | UC-19 |
| BR-32 | An unused day pass expires at the end of the day. | UC-19 |
| BR-33 | If a customer with a package of one month or longer has no check-in photo yet (for example after buying online), the Receptionist takes the photo at the first check-in before completing it. | UC-19 |
| BR-34 | A membership package (one month or longer) allows unlimited check-ins within its validity, including several entries on the same day. Only the day pass is limited to a single entry (CBR-36, BR-29). | UC-19 |
| BR-35 | PT package sessions fall only on Monday to Friday. This is a core rule of the term-based PT package (BR-40), not only of the initial scheduling step. The gym itself opens at the weekend like any other day: check-in, day passes, counter sales, single sessions and swapped sessions all work normally on Saturday and Sunday; only the fixed schedule generated for a PT package skips them. | UC-21 |
| BR-36 | Saturday and Sunday are shown on the scheduling calendar but cannot be selected. | UC-21 |
| BR-37 | Both members of a couple package must hold a valid membership package when the order is created (CBR-59). A person with only a day pass, or with an expired or frozen membership, cannot join a couple package. | UC-21 |
| BR-38 | The PT consults the customer in person before the package is sold. | UC-21 |
| BR-39 | The customer chooses the PT; the PT cannot choose or refuse a customer. | UC-21 |
| BR-40 | A PT package runs by term: the Receptionist picks the start date and the system computes end date \= start date \+ package duration, last day inclusive (GBR-03). The system generates a session for every Monday-to-Friday within the term at the one fixed slot chosen (CBR-43), except declared closed days (CBR-56) and days needing another time (BR-41). No make-up sessions, no term extension. The number of generated sessions is fixed and stored on the subscription when the order is Paid. | UC-21 |
| BR-41 | If the fixed slot is already taken on some dates within the term, the Receptionist picks another free slot of the same PT for those dates only. If no alternative is free, that date has no session and no make-up (as in CBR-56). | UC-21 |
| BR-42 | An order can use at most one voucher. | UC-23 |
| BR-43 | When a voucher is applied successfully, its used count increases by one. | UC-23 |
| BR-44 | When an order with a voucher is Cancelled for any reason (CBR-11, CBR-70, CBR-71, CBR-72), one use of the voucher is returned. | UC-23 |
| BR-45 | When a customer removes a voucher from a Pending order or replaces it, one use of the old voucher is returned. | UC-23 |
| BR-46 | The Receptionist can close a shift only after entering the counted cash; if it differs from the expected cash (DBR-55), a reason is required. | UC-25 |
| BR-47 | Money from transactions under CBR-72 is refunded to the customer by the Manager outside the system. | UC-26 |
| BR-48 | Only the Receptionist closes a maintenance request (In Progress → Closed), after checking that the item has been repaired. | UC-28 |
| BR-49 | Only the Manager approves (Open → In Progress) or rejects (Open → Rejected) a maintenance request. | UC-29 |
| BR-50 | The number of sessions a PT teaches per day is decided by the PT when publishing availability; the system sets no limit. | UC-30 |
| BR-51 | A PT may publish availability for any future date, without a limit on weeks or months ahead. | UC-30 |
| BR-52 | A customer who does not show up without notice has the session deducted. | UC-31 |
| BR-53 | For a couple package, deductions are made from the shared quota regardless of who is absent. | UC-31 |
| BR-54 | The PT can mark an absence only from the session start until 24 hours after the session ends. | UC-31 |
| BR-55 | When the customer does not come, the PT presses Absent once; the session becomes Missed and is deducted immediately. | UC-31 |
| BR-56 | For a couple package the PT may mark an absence only when both members are absent; if either member attends, the session is Completed. | UC-31 |
| BR-57 | The PT does not approve or reject individual sessions of a confirmed package schedule. | UC-32 |
| BR-58 | A PT can edit their own note about a client at any time; saving overwrites the current note. | UC-33 |
| BR-59 | A PT can delete their own note about a client. The note is hidden permanently (soft delete, GBR-05) and the PT can then write a new note for that client. | UC-33 |
| BR-60 | A PT can edit a workout or meal plan they created at any time. Edits to a published plan reach the customer only when the PT publishes again; the customer always sees the latest published version. | UC-34 |
| BR-61 | A PT can delete a workout or meal plan they created. It disappears from the customer's My Plan screen immediately (soft delete, GBR-05), and the PT can then write a new plan of that type for the client. | UC-34 |
| BR-62 | A PT reschedules a PT session at the request of a customer without an account through a dedicated option on the session-handling screen (different from rescheduling because the PT is busy — BR-64). It is logged as a swap and counts toward the 3-swap limit (BR-73); CBR-44 and BR-74 still apply, while BR-75 and CBR-39 do not — any weekday and any week can be chosen, as when the Receptionist schedules. | UC-35 |
| BR-63 | A PT who cannot teach a session must contact the customer and agree on one of three options — move it to another of the PT's own slots, transfer it to another PT, or cancel it with a cash refund — before acting in the system. | UC-35 |
| BR-64 | Reschedule: the session moves to another free slot of the same PT and stays Scheduled; it is not deducted and does not count as a customer swap. The target slot must lie within the PT package term — it cannot be moved past the end date (BR-40). | UC-35 |
| BR-65 | Transfer: the session moves to a free slot of another PT chosen by the customer and stays Scheduled; it is not deducted and does not count as a swap. | UC-35 |
| BR-66 | Cancel: the session becomes Cancelled; a reason and the tick 'customer agreed to a cash refund' are mandatory. The system creates no refund transaction. | UC-35 |
| BR-67 | The money for a session cancelled under BR-66 is returned to the customer in cash by the PT, outside the system. | UC-35 |
| BR-68 | When a session is transferred, the customer may choose any PT free at that time, regardless of price. The session value is unchanged, nothing is charged or refunded, and the commission for that session goes to the new PT. | UC-35 |
| BR-69 | A PT who cannot teach a session must handle it in the system (BR-64, BR-65 or BR-66) before the session starts. Violations are dealt with by the Manager outside the system. | UC-35 |
| BR-70 | Only the PT in charge may reschedule, transfer or cancel a session, and only while it is Scheduled and has not started. The Receptionist and Manager do not act on the PT's behalf. | UC-35 |
| BR-71 | A session cancelled under BR-66 is still deducted from the package, because the customer has been repaid in cash. | UC-35 |
| BR-72 | A member with canUseService \= FALSE cannot book a single PT session. | UC-37 |
| BR-73 | Each PT package allows at most P-08 swaps (default 3), counted per package, not per session. | UC-38 |
| BR-74 | A single session cannot be swapped. | UC-38 |
| BR-75 | When swapping, only Saturday or Sunday can be chosen; Monday to Friday are shown but disabled. The target slot must also lie within the PT package term (BR-40) — a session cannot be swapped past the end date. | UC-38 |
| BR-76 | Only a session that has not started yet can be swapped. A session that is already in progress or in the past, or that is no longer Scheduled (Completed, Missed or Cancelled), can no longer be moved; the customer contacts the PT instead. | UC-38 |
| BR-77 | Either member of a couple package may swap, regardless of who is the holder. | UC-38 |
| BR-78 | A swap on a couple package does not need the other member's confirmation. | UC-38 |
| BR-79 | A session cancelled by the customer is still deducted and never refunded, however early it is cancelled. | UC-39 |
| BR-80 | When a transaction becomes Success the order becomes Paid immediately, provided the order is not Cancelled and the amount equals the amount payable. | UC-PAY |

| Orders.CancelType | PaymentTimeout, ReplacedByNewOrder, InvalidPayment, CancelledByReceptionist |
| Packages.DurationUnit | Day, Month |
| AuditLogs.ActingRole | Admin, Manager, PT, Receptionist, Customer |

 

## **6\. System Messages** {#6.-system-messages}

| \# | Message code | Message Type | Context | Content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | MSG01 | In line | Search or filter returns nothing | No results found. Try different keywords or clear some filters. |
| 2 | MSG02 | In line | List has no records yet | No {object} yet. |
| 3 | MSG03 | In line | Report or history has no data in the selected range | No data in the selected time range. |
| 4 | MSG04 | Toast (error) | Unexpected server error | The system is busy. Please try again in a few minutes. |
| 5 | MSG05 | Toast (warning) | Network connection lost | Connection lost. Check your network and try again. |
| 6 | MSG06 | Dialog | Session has expired | Your session has expired. Please sign in again. |
| 7 | MSG07 | In line | User opens a screen outside their role | You do not have permission to access this function. |
| 8 | MSG08 | In line | Opening a record that does not exist or was deleted | This {object} could not be found. |
| 9 | MSG09 | In red, under the text box | Required field left empty | {Field\_name} is required. |
| 10 | MSG10 | In red, under the text box | Input longer than allowed | Exceed max length of {max\_length}. |
| 11 | MSG11 | In red, under the text box | Email format is invalid | Invalid email format. |
| 12 | MSG12 | In red, under the text box | Email already used by another active profile or account | This email is already used by another account. |

| 15 | MSG15 | In red, under the text box | Date of birth in the future | Date of birth cannot be in the future. |
| 16 | MSG16 | In red, under the text box | Date range reversed | The start date must be on or before the end date. |
| 17 | MSG17 | In red, under the text box | Numeric field holds text or a value ≤ 0 | Enter a number greater than 0\. |

## 

## **7\. Other Requirements** {#7.-other-requirements}

| ID | Category | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-01 | Technology stack | Java 17; Jakarta Servlet 6.0 / JSP with JSTL 3.0 (MVC: Servlet – Service – DAO); Apache Tomcat 10.1; Microsoft SQL Server with mssql-jdbc 13.4; jBCrypt 0.4 for password hashing; Gson 2.11 for JSON; Angus Mail 2.0 (SMTP) for email; Apache POI 5.3 for Excel export; JUnit 5 for unit tests; Maven build; Git / GitHub for source control. |
| NFR-02 | External services | VNPay payment gateway (sandbox) for online payment; an SMTP mailbox for verification codes and notifications; Open-Meteo weather API for the PT dashboard. When an external service is unavailable the related feature shows an error message and the rest of the system keeps working. |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The interface is in Vietnamese; dates dd/mm/yyyy, times 24-hour, money in VND with thousand separators (GBR-01, GBR-02, GBR-29). Every error is shown as a message from section System Messages, next to the field it concerns. |
| NFR-04 | Compatibility | The web application is used on current versions of Chrome, Edge and Firefox on desktop or laptop screens; the screens used on the gym floor (PT dashboard, session attendance) also fit a phone screen (GBR-35). |
| NFR-05 | Security | Passwords are stored only as BCrypt hashes and are never shown or logged (DBR-02). Every page except the public pages requires sign-in, and every request is checked against the role the user is working in (GBR-10, GBR-13). A sign-in session expires after 2 hours without activity (GBR-31). Database access uses parameterised queries only. |
| NFR-06 | Data integrity and retention | No business record is physically deleted (GBR-05). A deleted customer profile keeps its row as Inactive together with its orders, transactions, subscriptions, check-ins and sessions, so revenue and tax records stay complete. Sensitive actions are written to the audit log (GBR-07, GBR-08). |
| NFR-07 | Performance | Under normal use at one gym, a screen opens and a save completes within a few seconds; lists are paged (10 rows by default, GBR-18). |
| NFR-08 | Constraints | The system serves one gym. There is no SMS, no mobile app, no e-invoice and no in-system refund; these are handled outside the system (GBR-15, GBR-16). |
